evidence.explanation: Places this disease within the trigeminal autonomic cephalalgias, which is what licenses applying the shared mechanism above to it.

steps/0.description: The systems-level mechanism shared across the trigeminal autonomic cephalalgias: trigeminal nociceptive input and cranial parasympathetic outflow are abnormally coupled, so pain and autonomic features arrive together and on the same side. The proposed substrate involves hypothalamic dysfunction together with trigeminovascular, trigeminocervical, trigeminoautonomic, circadian and nociceptive circuitry. This is an inferred systems account rather than a demonstrated molecular one, and the node is pitched at that level deliberately.

evidence.snippet: Hemicrania continua is an uncommon primary headache disorder, characterized by continuous unilateral pain, where pain exacerbations are associated with cranial autonomic features.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the continuous background pain and the association of exacerbations with autonomic features, which is the structure this node describes.

evidence.snippet: Thirty-six (92%) patients had side-locked pain and 3 (8%) had side-alternating pain.
evidence.explanation: Quantifies the exception to side-locking. Curated because a feature described as characteristic is absent in roughly one patient in twelve, and a strict reading would misclassify them.

steps/1.description: The background pain is continuous and does not remit, which distinguishes this from the episodic trigeminal autonomic cephalalgias, and severe exacerbations are superimposed on it. The pain is characteristically side-locked, though a small minority of patients have side-alternating pain, which is worth recording because side-locking is often treated as definitional.

evidence.snippet: Hemicrania Continua (HC) is a rare and disabling primary headache disorder that is characterized by persistent, unilateral headache with ipsilateral, cranial autonomic symptoms and restlessness or agitation.
evidence.explanation: Names the ipsilateral confinement of the autonomic symptoms and the restlessness that accompanies exacerbations.

steps/2.description: Parasympathetic and sympathetic signs on the same side as the pain: tearing, conjunctival injection, nasal congestion, ptosis and miosis. Their ipsilateral confinement is mechanistically informative, since a systemic autonomic disturbance would not respect the midline, and it is what places the disorder among the trigeminal autonomic cephalalgias rather than among the migraines.

evidence.snippet: The core clinical features have been well described: unilateral, side-locked headaches that are continuous (although interrupted by frequent severe exacerbations), associated with autonomic symptoms and a response to indomethacin.
evidence.explanation: Enumerates the core features in one sentence, including the continuity, the exacerbations, and the indomethacin response.

steps/3.description: Continuous, strictly unilateral head pain with superimposed severe exacerbations, persisting without remission. The continuity is the feature that separates this from the episodic trigeminal autonomic cephalalgias.

evidence.snippet: Of the cohort, 97% had at least one cranial autonomic feature during exacerbations: 73% had lacrimation, 51% nasal congestion, 46% conjunctival injection and 40% ptosis and facial flushing.
evidence.explanation: Names lacrimation directly and puts it at 73 per cent of the cohort, the commonest autonomic feature, which supports both the phenotype and the FREQUENT band. This replaces an earlier citation that established only that cranial autonomic features occur as a class.

steps/4.description: Tearing on the painful side during exacerbations, one of the cranial autonomic features.

evidence.snippet: Of the cohort, 97% had at least one cranial autonomic feature during exacerbations: 73% had lacrimation, 51% nasal congestion, 46% conjunctival injection and 40% ptosis and facial flushing.
evidence.explanation: Names nasal congestion directly at 51 per cent of the cohort.

steps/5.description: Nasal blockage or rhinorrhoea on the painful side, from parasympathetic activation of the nasal mucosa.

evidence.snippet: Of the cohort, 97% had at least one cranial autonomic feature during exacerbations: 73% had lacrimation, 51% nasal congestion, 46% conjunctival injection and 40% ptosis and facial flushing.
evidence.explanation: Names ptosis directly at 40 per cent, reported together with facial flushing at the same rate.

steps/6.description: Drooping of the upper lid on the painful side, part of the partial Horner-like picture that can accompany exacerbations.

evidence.snippet: Other cranial autonomic features included rhinorrhoea, forehead/facial sweating, itching eye, eyelid oedema, sense of aural fullness and periaural swelling, miosis, mydriasis and swelling of the cheek and face.
evidence.explanation: Names miosis directly, in the unquantified tail of the autonomic list rather than among the four features given percentages.

steps/7.description: Pupillary constriction on the painful side, the other half of the partial Horner-like picture.

evidence.snippet: In addition, about two-thirds were agitated or restless, or both, and about one-quarter were aggressive, mainly verbally, with severe pain.
evidence.explanation: Quantifies the feature at about two-thirds of the cohort, which supports the FREQUENT band, and records the aggression at the severe end as well.

steps/8.description: Pacing, rocking, an inability to keep still during an exacerbation. This is not incidental distress: ICHD-3 admits it as an alternative to cranial autonomic features in the diagnostic criteria, so a patient with no visible autonomic sign can still meet the definition on this alone. It also carries diagnostic weight in the other direction, since the migraine patient this disease is most often mistaken for characteristically lies still in the dark.

evidence.snippet: In addition, about two-thirds were agitated or restless, or both, and about one-quarter were aggressive, mainly verbally, with severe pain.
evidence.explanation: PARTIAL because the source counts agitated OR restless OR both as one figure, so two-thirds is a combined rate rather than a rate for agitation alone. The band is an upper bound on this term.

steps/9.description: The agitated pole of the same restlessness, reported together with it in the source and separated here only because HPO codes the two distinctly.

evidence.snippet: Of the cohort, 97% had at least one cranial autonomic feature during exacerbations: 73% had lacrimation, 51% nasal congestion, 46% conjunctival injection and 40% ptosis and facial flushing.
evidence.explanation: Names conjunctival injection at 46 per cent of the cohort.

steps/10.description: Redness of the eye on the painful side, one of the quantified cranial autonomic features.

evidence.snippet: Thirty-one (79%) had phonophobia, which was unilateral in 14 (48%); 29 (74%) had photophobia, which was unilateral in 14 (48%); and 27 (69%) had motion sensitivity.
evidence.explanation: Puts phonophobia at 79 per cent, the commonest feature in the cohort after the pain itself. Note the detail that it was UNILATERAL in about half: unilateral phonophobia is not a migraine feature, so the same symptom that causes the misdiagnosis can, examined properly, help undo it.

steps/11.description: Sound sensitivity, and one of the two features that make this disease look like chronic migraine. Its presence is a large part of why patients wait years for the diagnosis, so it belongs in the phenotype list rather than only in the differential.

evidence.snippet: Thirty-one (79%) had phonophobia, which was unilateral in 14 (48%); 29 (74%) had photophobia, which was unilateral in 14 (48%); and 27 (69%) had motion sensitivity.
evidence.explanation: Puts photophobia at 74 per cent, unilateral in about half.

steps/12.description: Light sensitivity, the other migraine-mimicking feature, and unilateral in about half of those who have it.

edges/1.description: Parasympathetic outflow coupled to the nociceptive traffic, producing autonomic signs on the painful side.

This is the feature ICHD-3 accepts in place of autonomic signs, so it belongs on the pain arm of the graph rather than the autonomic one.

Nothing cited here establishes the route, and the intermediates are marked unknown for that reason; the reason to model it at all is that it is present in three-quarters of patients and drives the migraine misdiagnosis.

evidence.snippet: The hallmark of this condition is the absolute response to indometacin.
evidence.explanation: The efficacy claim, quoted from a clinical series. Note the circularity recorded in the description: this is also the criterion by which the series was assembled.

treatments/0.description: Simultaneously the treatment and the diagnostic test, which is why its apparent efficacy must be read carefully. Response is characteristically rapid and complete. But because an absolute response is part of the case definition, every diagnosed patient is a responder by construction, and the literature reporting near-universal efficacy is describing the definition rather than measuring an effect. The drug is genuinely effective; the evidence for it is circular, and both things are true.

evidence.snippet: The diagnosis requires patients to experience an absolute response to therapeutic doses of indomethacin.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the completeness of the response, which is what makes this a mechanism-level effect rather than analgesia.

treatments/0/targets/0.description: Acts on the mechanism rather than the symptom, though how is not established. Indomethacin's distinctive activity in this disorder is not shared by other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, which argues that cyclo-oxygenase inhibition alone does not account for it.

evidence.snippet: The COX-2 inhibitors (celecoxib and rofecoxib,), piroxicam derivative and topiramate are the main drugs found to be effective in patients with HC.
evidence.explanation: Names the alternatives and identifies COX-2 inhibitors as the main effective class.

evidence.snippet: Incidence and prevalence of indomethacin-related side effects in patients with HC vary between 20% and 75%.
evidence.explanation: The reason alternatives are needed at all, and the figure that makes indomethacin-only management untenable for a large minority.

treatments/1.description: The treatment question that matters in practice, and the one an indomethacin-only entry hides. Indomethacin works, but between a fifth and three-quarters of patients develop side effects on it, and it is not a safe drug to take indefinitely. So the real clinical problem is not whether indomethacin works, it is what to do for the substantial fraction who cannot keep taking it. The alternatives are COX-2 inhibitors, a piroxicam derivative, and topiramate, with melatonin as an adjunct. All of them are supported by case reports and open-label series rather than trials, and none responds predictably in an individual patient, which is a real limitation and not a hedge.

evidence.snippet: However, the effects of all these drugs are not uniform and consistent in each patient.
evidence.explanation: PARTIAL by the source's own statement: these drugs work in some patients and not others, and which is which cannot be predicted.

treatments/1/targets/0.description: Directed at the same mechanism as indomethacin without reproducing its completeness of effect. That partial, inconsistent response is itself evidence about the mechanism, and it is what the entry's knowledge gap turns on.

open_questions/0.rationale: A definition built on a therapeutic response has a blind spot by construction. Patients with continuous unilateral headache, ipsilateral cranial autonomic features and no indomethacin response are excluded from the entity, and where they go is unclear: they may have a distinct disorder, a variant of the same mechanism with a different pharmacology, or the same disease inadequately dosed. This is not merely taxonomic. If the underlying mechanism is what the trigeminal autonomic account describes, then indomethacin responsiveness is a property of one subgroup and the entity is narrower than the biology. Resolving it would require studying the excluded patients, who by definition are not in any hemicrania continua cohort.

open_questions/1.rationale: The selectivity is the clue and it is unexplained. State it carefully, because an earlier revision of this rationale overstated it and its own cached source contradicted it. Other cyclo-oxygenase inhibitors are NOT inert here: COX-2 inhibitors are described as the main effective alternatives for patients who cannot tolerate indomethacin. What they do not reproduce is the ABSOLUTE and predictable response that defines the disease, since their effects are explicitly not uniform or consistent between patients. So the puzzle is not that the class does nothing, it is that one member of the class does something categorically different from the rest. Proposed explanations have included effects on nitric oxide signalling, on intracranial pressure, and on cerebral blood flow, none established. This matters beyond curiosity: the mechanism of the defining drug is the most direct available probe of the mechanism of the disease, and a disorder identified by a drug response with no account of why that drug works has a hole at its centre.

evidence.snippet: Type I and II HAE result from a mutation in the SERPING1 gene, which encodes C1-INH.
evidence.explanation: Review evidence supports SERPING1 as the classic HAE causal gene.

evidence.snippet: C1-INH is important in the coagulation complement, contact systems, and fibrinolysis.
evidence.explanation: Review evidence supports the regulated pathways affected by C1-INH deficiency.

steps/3.description: SERPING1 pathogenic variants cause quantitative C1-INH deficiency in type 1 HAE or qualitative C1-INH dysfunction in type 2 HAE, reducing regulation of complement, coagulation, fibrinolytic, and contact-system cascades.

evidence.snippet: proven genetic pathogenic variants that co-segregate with angioedema expression within families.
evidence.explanation: Consensus evidence supports familial pathogenic variants in normal-C1-INH HAE.

evidence.snippet: underlying mutations such as in kininogen-1 (HAE-KNG1), plasminogen gene (PLG-HAE), myoferlin gene mutation (MYOF-HAE), heparan sulfate-glucosamine 3-sulfotransferase 6 (HS3ST6), mutation in Hageman factor (factor XII), and in angiopoietin-1 (HAE-ANGPT-1).
evidence.explanation: Review evidence lists the normal-C1-INH genetic heterogeneity captured in this node.

steps/4.description: Normal-C1-INH HAE includes genetically defined non-mast-cell angioedema families with F12, PLG, KNG1, ANGPT1, HS3ST6, MYOF, or other variants that converge on bradykinin-mediated or contact-system angioedema biology. The subtype genes enter the shared pathograph at different points rather than through one common step: F12 gain of function amplifies contact activation, KNG1 alters the bradykinin cleavage site of its own substrate, PLG variants act through the plasmin arm, and ANGPT1 and HS3ST6 act on the endothelial barrier itself. Whether every normal-C1-INH subtype is strictly bradykinin-mediated is not established.

evidence.snippet: As C1 inhibitor also possesses a central regulatory role of other plasma systems, including the contact activation system of coagulation and the plasminogen-plasmin system that governs endogenous fibrinolysis
evidence.explanation: Establishes C1-INH regulation of the plasminogen-plasmin system alongside the contact system.

evidence.snippet: We detected a mutation in the plasminogen (PLG) gene in patients with HAEnCI.
evidence.explanation: Supports a plasminogen-dependent route to normal-C1-INH HAE.

steps/5.description: C1-INH restrains the plasminogen-plasmin (fibrinolytic) system in addition to the contact system, and plasmin can feed back into contact activation and kinin generation. This arm is the mechanistic rationale for the PLG-related normal-C1-INH subtype and for the historical use of the antifibrinolytic tranexamic acid, and it underlies the raised D-dimer seen during attacks.

evidence.snippet: This cascade of events resulted in Ca2+ overload, disruption of mitochondrial structure and function, and eventually triggered apoptosis.
evidence.explanation: Documents the ER-retention consequences in a cellular model of a SERPING1 variant.

evidence.snippet: Using siRNA to knock down GRP75 mitigates cellular calcium overload and mitochondrial damage induced by the SERPING1 mutation.
evidence.explanation: Rescue by GRP75 knockdown supports GRP75 as the mediator of the retention phenotype.

steps/6.description: A subset of SERPING1 missense variants are not simply null alleles: the mutant C1-INH protein is retained and aggregates in the endoplasmic reticulum. In a reported Han Chinese family the c.708T>G variant raised intracellular C1-INH, upregulated GRP75, and produced calcium overload, mitochondrial damage, and apoptosis. This arm is a proposed cell-intrinsic contributor and biomarker route rather than an established driver of the swelling itself, which remains bradykinin-mediated.

evidence.snippet: Hereditary angioedema is a rare and potentially life-threatening genetic disease that is associated with kallikrein-kinin system dysregulation.
evidence.explanation: The pivotal FXIIa-inhibitor trial frames HAE as a kallikrein-kinin dysregulation disorder, supporting contact-system activation as a core mechanism node.

evidence.snippet: Bradykinin, which is considered to be a byproduct of the plasma contact system during in vitro coagulation, is the main disease mediator in HAE.
evidence.explanation: Places the plasma contact system upstream of bradykinin, the main HAE mediator.

steps/9.description: With C1-INH absent or dysfunctional, factor XII autoactivates to factor XIIa without adequate inhibition. FXIIa is the apex protease of the plasma contact (kallikrein-kinin) system in HAE, and gain-of-function F12 variants produce the same excess activation in F12-related normal-C1-INH disease. FXIIa is a validated drug target: the anti-FXIIa antibody garadacimab prevents attacks.

evidence.snippet: Ecallantide, a novel plasma kallikrein inhibitor, inhibits production of bradykinin, the key mediator of these angioedema attacks.
evidence.explanation: Establishes plasma kallikrein as the protease whose inhibition blocks bradykinin production in HAE.

evidence.snippet: As C1 inhibitor also possesses a central regulatory role of other plasma systems, including the contact activation system of coagulation and the plasminogen-plasmin system that governs endogenous fibrinolysis
evidence.explanation: Supports C1-INH regulation of the contact and fibrinolytic systems that converge on kallikrein activity.

steps/10.description: Active plasma kallikrein is the central effector protease of the HAE cascade. It cleaves high-molecular-weight kininogen to liberate bradykinin and also reciprocally activates more factor XII, creating a self-amplifying loop that explains the explosive, self-sustaining character of attacks. Plasma kallikrein is the most heavily drugged node in HAE: ecallantide, lanadelumab, berotralstat, and sebetralstat inhibit the active enzyme, while donidalorsen lowers the prekallikrein zymogen pool.

evidence.snippet: excessive bradykinin production, with subsequent increased vascular permeability
evidence.explanation: Supports excess bradykinin generation as the step preceding increased permeability.

steps/11.description: Kallikrein-mediated proteolysis of high-molecular-weight kininogen (the KNG1 gene product) releases the nonapeptide bradykinin. Cleaved kininogen is a contact-activation biomarker, and a KNG1 variant altering the N-terminal bradykinin cleavage site causes a normal-C1-INH HAE subtype, placing this step directly on the disease path.

evidence.snippet: excessive bradykinin production, with subsequent increased vascular permeability
evidence.explanation: Review evidence directly supports the bradykinin-to-permeability mechanism.

evidence.snippet: Icatibant is a selective bradykinin B2 receptor antagonist.
evidence.explanation: Efficacy of a selective B2 receptor antagonist supports B2 receptor engagement as the operative bradykinin signalling step.

evidence.snippet: Bradykinin is the key mediator of symptoms.
evidence.explanation: Randomized-trial background identifies bradykinin as the mediator of HAE symptoms.

steps/12.description: Excess bradykinin is the central mediator of HAE attacks. It acts on the bradykinin B2 receptor on vascular endothelium to increase permeability in superficial tissues and gastrointestinal and respiratory mucosa. The B2 receptor is the target of icatibant; the contribution of the bradykinin B1 receptor remains unresolved and is recorded as a knowledge gap.

evidence.snippet: This knowledge is driving increased attention to the role of endothelial biology in determining disease activity in hereditary angioedema.
evidence.explanation: Supports endothelial biology as the determinant of HAE disease activity, justifying a dedicated endothelial node.

evidence.snippet: Likewise, cell surface expression of β-catenin was reduced and severe gap formation between adjacent HUVECs developed.
evidence.explanation: Endothelial-cell experiments demonstrate junctional protein loss and gap formation, the cellular readout of this node.

evidence.snippet: The ANGPT1 reduced ability to counteract the increment of endothelial permeability produced by inducers, such as VEGF and bradykinin, stimulate vascular leakage and reorganization of the F-actin cytoskeletal elements.
evidence.explanation: Links ANGPT1 loss of function to failure of counter-regulation against bradykinin-induced endothelial leak.

steps/13.description: The proximate cellular lesion of an HAE attack is loss of interendothelial adherens junction integrity in postcapillary vessels, with reduced VE-cadherin and beta-catenin at the cell surface, F-actin stress-fibre reorganization, and interendothelial gap formation. This node is the point of convergence for the bradykinin-mediated arm and for the normal-C1-INH "endothelial barrier" genes: ANGPT1 haploinsufficiency impairs the Tie2-dependent counter-regulation that normally opposes bradykinin- and VEGF-induced leak, and HS3ST6 loss alters endothelial heparan sulfate involved in cell-surface interactions of angioedema mediators.

evidence.snippet: recurrent attacks of nonpitting edema of the skin, severe abdominal symptoms such as pain and swelling, and/or respiratory distress due to upper respiratory airways involvement.
evidence.explanation: Orphanet supports recurrent edema attacks involving skin, abdomen, and airway.

evidence.snippet: Patients present with prolonged attacks which last for approximately two to five days and may include nonpitting edema of the skin, severe abdominal symptoms such as pain and swelling, and/or respiratory distress due to upper respiratory airways involvement.

steps/14.description: Increased vascular permeability causes transitory, recurrent, nonpitting subcutaneous and submucosal edema attacks involving skin, abdomen, genital tissues, pharynx, and larynx. The lesion is interstitial fluid accumulation from postcapillary endothelial leak, not primary tissue destruction, which is why attacks resolve completely and leave no fibrosis or scarring.

treatments/0.description: Plasma-derived or recombinant C1-INH replacement restores the deficient regulator in C1-INH-deficiency HAE and can be used for long-term prophylaxis against attacks.

treatments/1.description: Icatibant is a bradykinin B2 receptor antagonist used as on-demand treatment for acute HAE attacks.

evidence.snippet: Icatibant is a selective bradykinin B2 receptor antagonist.
evidence.explanation: Trial background directly states the drug mechanism.

treatments/1/targets/0.description: Icatibant blocks bradykinin B2 receptor signaling during an acute attack.

evidence.explanation: Integrated phase 3 evidence supports ecallantide efficacy for acute attacks.

treatments/2.description: Ecallantide inhibits plasma kallikrein and thereby reduces bradykinin production during acute HAE attacks.

evidence.snippet: Ecallantide, a novel plasma kallikrein inhibitor, inhibits production of bradykinin, the key mediator of these angioedema attacks.
evidence.explanation: Integrated phase 3 evidence states the drug mechanism.

treatments/2/targets/0.description: Plasma kallikrein inhibition reduces bradykinin generation during attacks.

evidence.snippet: No new safety signals were observed, and effectiveness for repeated attacks was consistent with the KONFIDENT trial results.
evidence.explanation: Extension evidence supports repeated-attack effectiveness of sebetralstat.

treatments/3.description: Sebetralstat is an oral plasma kallikrein inhibitor for on-demand treatment of HAE attacks due to C1-INH deficiency.

evidence.snippet: Sebetralstat, an oral plasma kallikrein inhibitor
evidence.explanation: Open-label extension evidence states the oral kallikrein-inhibitor mechanism.

treatments/3/targets/0.description: Oral kallikrein inhibition reduces attack-associated bradykinin signaling.

evidence.snippet: treatment with subcutaneous lanadelumab for 26 weeks significantly reduced the attack rate compared with placebo.
evidence.explanation: Randomized trial evidence supports lanadelumab prophylaxis.

treatments/4.description: Lanadelumab is a fully human monoclonal antibody that selectively inhibits active plasma kallikrein, given subcutaneously for long-term prophylaxis. It is split from berotralstat here despite sharing a target: the two differ in modality, route and dosing interval in ways that drive real clinical choice, and bundling them made per-drug modality tagging impossible.

evidence.snippet: lanadelumab, a fully human monoclonal antibody that selectively inhibits active plasma kallikrein
evidence.explanation: Phase 3 trial evidence states the lanadelumab mechanism.

treatments/4/targets/0.description: Direct plasma kallikrein inhibition reduces bradykinin generation upstream of edema attacks.

evidence.snippet: Berotralstat (BCX7353) is a recently approved, oral, once-daily kallikrein inhibitor for hereditary angioedema (HAE) prophylaxis.
evidence.explanation: APeX-2 evidence supports oral berotralstat prophylaxis.

treatments/5.description: Berotralstat is an orally administered, once-daily small-molecule plasma kallikrein inhibitor for long-term prophylaxis. Same molecular target as lanadelumab, different platform - which is precisely why the two are curated separately.

evidence.snippet: Berotralstat (BCX7353) is a recently approved, oral, once-daily kallikrein inhibitor for hereditary angioedema (HAE) prophylaxis.
evidence.explanation: Names the drug's molecular target directly, which is exactly what this edge asserts: berotralstat acts on the plasma kallikrein node by inhibiting kallikrein itself.

treatments/5/targets/0.description: Oral small-molecule kallikrein inhibition reduces bradykinin generation upstream of edema attacks.

evidence.snippet: Effective treatments included C1 inhibitor concentrate for angioedema attacks (6 women) and, for prophylaxis, progesterone (8 women), danazol (2 women), and tranexamic acid (1 woman).
evidence.explanation: Documents danazol as effective prophylaxis in hereditary angioedema. PARTIAL, and the limits matter: this is an FXII-HAE (normal C1-INH) cohort and only two women received danazol, so it is not the randomized evidence that underpins the modern agents in this entry.

evidence.snippet: Attenuated androgens can reduce the number and severity of attacks when used prophylactically but have important adverse effects and are ineffective during acute attacks.
evidence.explanation: Prophylaxis-specific support for the attenuated-androgen class, and the stronger of the two items attached here: it states the prophylactic benefit and both of the limitations that put danazol behind the targeted agents. Tagged OTHER because the sentence is background framing in the introduction to an icatibant trial report, summarizing prior evidence rather than reporting that trial's own data.

treatments/6.description: Danazol is the historical mainstay of long-term prophylaxis and remains in guideline algorithms as a second-line option where modern targeted agents are unavailable or unaffordable - which is most of the world. It works indirectly, raising hepatic C1-INH and C4 production rather than blocking the contact cascade, and it is the only prophylactic option in this entry that acts by increasing the deficient protein rather than inhibiting a downstream enzyme. Its displacement by kallikrein-targeted agents is driven by tolerability - androgenic effects, dyslipidaemia, hepatic adenoma and virilisation risk - rather than by lack of efficacy.

treatments/6/targets/0.description: Attenuated androgens are thought to raise circulating C1-INH rather than inhibiting a downstream enzyme, which is why they are placed on the deficiency node itself. The hedge is deliberate: the prophylactic benefit is well attested, but the mechanism by which attenuated androgens produce it is not fully settled.

evidence.snippet: Effective treatments included C1 inhibitor concentrate for angioedema attacks (6 women) and, for prophylaxis, progesterone (8 women), danazol (2 women), and tranexamic acid (1 woman).
evidence.explanation: Documents tranexamic acid as effective prophylaxis in hereditary angioedema. PARTIAL and thinly so: a single patient in an FXII-HAE cohort. It is curated because the drug closes a treatment join point on the plasmin node that would otherwise have no intervention attached, not because this observation is strong.

treatments/7.description: An antifibrinolytic used for long-term prophylaxis, chiefly where attenuated androgens are contraindicated - notably in children and in pregnancy. It is the treatment that gives the plasmin amplification arm of this pathograph its therapeutic rationale: by inhibiting plasmin, it blocks the plasmin-mediated feedback that amplifies contact-system activation, rather than acting on kallikrein or bradykinin directly. Efficacy is modest compared with the targeted agents.

treatments/7/targets/0.description: Antifibrinolytic blockade of plasmin interrupts the plasmin-driven amplification loop that feeds contact-system activation - the mechanism this node describes and the reason tranexamic acid is used at all.

evidence.snippet: During the 6-month treatment period (day 1 to day 182), the mean number of investigator-confirmed hereditary angioedema attacks per month was significantly lower in the garadacimab group
evidence.explanation: Phase 3 randomized trial evidence supports garadacimab prophylaxis efficacy.

treatments/8.description: Garadacimab (CSL312) is a fully human monoclonal antibody that inhibits activated factor XII (FXIIa), given once monthly by subcutaneous injection for long-term prophylaxis of HAE attacks. Mechanistically it is distinctive in acting at the apex of the contact cascade rather than at plasma kallikrein or the bradykinin receptor. In the pivotal VANGUARD phase 3 trial in type I and type II HAE it lowered the monthly attack rate significantly versus placebo, a mean difference of -87%.

evidence.snippet: Garadacimab (CSL312), a novel, fully-human monoclonal antibody that inhibits activated factor XII (FXIIa), is being studied for the prevention of hereditary angioedema attacks.
evidence.explanation: States that garadacimab inhibits activated factor XII, the mechanism of this treatment edge.

treatments/8/targets/0.description: Garadacimab binds and inhibits activated factor XII, blocking the apex protease of the contact system and preventing downstream kallikrein activation and bradykinin generation.

evidence.snippet: Donidalorsen demonstrated sustained reductions in HAE attack rate, improvements in QoL, and an acceptable safety profile after 1 year of treatment.
evidence.explanation: OASISplus extension evidence supports donidalorsen long-term prophylaxis.

evidence.snippet: donidalorsen treatment resulted in a significantly lower rate of angioedema attacks than placebo in this small, phase 2 trial.
evidence.explanation: Phase 2 randomized trial evidence supports donidalorsen prophylactic efficacy.

treatments/9.description: Donidalorsen (Dawnzera) is a prekallikrein-directed antisense oligonucleotide approved for long-term prophylaxis of hereditary angioedema attacks. RNase H1-mediated knockdown of KLKB1 (prekallikrein) mRNA lowers plasma prekallikrein, reducing bradykinin generation upstream of edema attacks.

evidence.snippet: Donidalorsen, a prekallikrein-directed antisense oligonucleotide indicated for prophylaxis of hereditary angioedema (HAE) attacks
evidence.explanation: The trial report identifies donidalorsen as a prekallikrein-directed antisense oligonucleotide for HAE prophylaxis.

evidence.snippet: Selective inhibition of plasma prekallikrein production by antisense oligonucleotide treatment (donidalorsen) may reduce the frequency of attacks and the burden of disease.
evidence.explanation: Phase 2 trial background statement identifies donidalorsen as an antisense oligonucleotide that selectively suppresses prekallikrein production.

treatments/9/targets/0.description: Prekallikrein knockdown lowers the plasma prekallikrein pool available for conversion to active kallikrein, reducing bradykinin generation upstream of edema attacks.

evidence.snippet: Important areas that remain poorly understood include the factors that lead to very low plasma functional C1 inhibitor levels, the triggers of contact system activation in hereditary angioedema, and the role of the bradykinin B1 receptor.
evidence.explanation: Names the triggers of contact-system activation as an explicitly unresolved area.

evidence.snippet: In addition, it is questionable whether a surface is responsible for contact system activation in HAE.
evidence.explanation: States the open question of whether an activating surface is required in HAE.

open_questions/0.rationale: The pathograph downstream of contact activation is well established, but the initiating event is not. C1-INH deficiency is constant while attacks are episodic and localized, so something must license activation at a particular time and site. Classical models invoke an anionic activating surface for factor XII autoactivation, but it is questionable whether a surface is responsible in HAE, and the recognized clinical triggers (trauma, procedures, estrogens, stress) have no established molecular mapping onto the cascade. This gap is why attack prediction remains impossible and why prophylaxis must be continuous rather than targeted.

evidence.snippet: Important areas that remain poorly understood include the factors that lead to very low plasma functional C1 inhibitor levels, the triggers of contact system activation in hereditary angioedema, and the role of the bradykinin B1 receptor.
evidence.explanation: Explicitly names the role of the bradykinin B1 receptor as poorly understood.

open_questions/1.rationale: Icatibant establishes the B2 receptor as an operative and druggable target, but B2 blockade does not abolish all attacks and the B1 receptor is inducible under inflammatory conditions and mediates vascular hyperpermeability in other settings. If B1 signalling contributes, it would predict a therapeutic ceiling for B2-selective antagonism and identify a complementary target. The question is currently unresolved rather than negative.

evidence.snippet: The phenotypic variability of hereditary angioedema has been extensively documented but never understood.
evidence.explanation: States directly that HAE phenotypic variability remains unexplained.

open_questions/2.rationale: Attack burden ranges from essentially asymptomatic carriage to frequent life-threatening laryngeal attacks within the same family and the same variant, and C1-INH level does not predict it. No validated genetic, hormonal, or endothelial modifier explains this, which prevents risk-stratified prophylaxis and means treatment intensity is chosen on observed burden rather than predicted risk.

evidence.snippet: Despite extensive genetic analyses, the diagnostic yield for nC1-INH HAE remains low in our study, the pathogenic variant for nC1-INH HAE was identified in only 1 patient (n = 21).
evidence.explanation: Quantifies the low molecular diagnostic yield that defines this gap.

evidence.snippet: Investigation into candidate genes yielded no pathogenic variants, prompting a re-evaluation of patients' diagnoses.
evidence.explanation: Shows that negative testing led to diagnostic re-evaluation, supporting the overdiagnosis concern.

open_questions/3.rationale: Normal-C1-INH HAE has no confirmatory biochemical test, so diagnosis rests on clinical pattern plus a variant in one of a small gene set. Comprehensive sequencing resolves only a small minority of suspected cases, and broad testing generates variants of uncertain significance and risks overdiagnosis. Consequently management recommendations for this branch are largely expert opinion, and it is not established that every normal-C1-INH subtype is bradykinin-mediated at all.

evidence.snippet: We have identified mutations in three affected individuals: a C to G substitution converting a tyrosine to a termination codon, a 39 base pair deletion and a 2 basepair deletion which creates a premature termination codon.
evidence.explanation: Documents the initiating germline lesion and its truncating character.

steps/1.description: A heterozygous truncating or otherwise inactivating variant in ENG at 9q34 is inherited through the family. The founding alleles were a nonsense codon and two frameshifting deletions, so the primary lesion removes functional protein rather than altering its activity.

evidence.snippet: Endoglin (CD105), an accessory protein of the TGF-beta receptor superfamily, is highly expressed on endothelial cells.
evidence.explanation: Establishes endoglin's identity and endothelial expression, the substrate of this node.

steps/2.description: Endothelial cells carry roughly half the normal complement of endoglin, an accessory protein of the TGF-beta receptor superfamily that is highly expressed on endothelium. Mutant protein is largely absent from the cell surface, so the phenotype follows from reduced dosage of the wild-type product rather than from a dominant-negative species.

evidence.snippet: including the loss of heterozygosity in ENG in one brain AVM sample, in which the germline mutation occurred in a different allele than a nearby somatic mutation (both are loss-of-function mutations)
evidence.explanation: The ENG-specific demonstration of biallelic inactivation in a lesion, which is what makes this node HHT1 evidence rather than generic HHT evidence.

evidence.snippet: Patients with HHT harbor these heterozygous germline mutations in every cell of the body, yet vascular malformations occur in only a small minority of vessels, with predilection for specific anatomic locations.
evidence.explanation: States the focality problem that this node exists to solve.

evidence.snippet: Here, we show that another mechanism for the second hit is loss of heterozygosity across the chromosome bearing the germline mutation.
evidence.explanation: Adds loss of heterozygosity as a second route to biallelic inactivation alongside a somatic point mutation. Indirect because the paper works at the level of "an HHT gene" rather than reporting ENG separately.

evidence.snippet: We also identified somatic mutations in one pulmonary AVM and two brain AVMs, confirming that mucocutaneous and internal organ vascular malformations undergo the same molecular mechanisms.
evidence.explanation: Extends the second-hit mechanism to the pulmonary and cerebral lesions that dominate HHT1, rather than leaving it established only for skin telangiectases. Indirect for the same gene-agnostic reason.

steps/3.description: The germline variant is present in every cell, yet malformations form in only a small minority of vessels. A very-low-level somatic loss-of-function mutation on the second ENG allele within the lesional endothelium supplies the focal trigger. Loss of heterozygosity at ENG has been demonstrated in a brain AVM in which the germline and somatic loss-of-function mutations lay on different alleles. This node explains the focality and the intrafamilial variability that haploinsufficiency alone does not.

evidence.snippet: ENG and ACVRL1 are both required for angiogenesis and mutations in either gene are associated with Hereditary Hemorrhagic Telangectasia, a rare genetic vascular disorder.
evidence.explanation: Places ENG and ALK1 in one angiogenic pathway, which is what makes this a shared HHT1/HHT2 node. The source spells the disease "Telangectasia"; the snippet preserves the original text.

evidence.snippet: BMP9 interacts with a hydrophobic surface of the N-terminal orphan domain of ENG, which adopts a new duplicated fold generated by circular permutation. The interface involves residues mutated in HHT1 and overlaps with the epitope of tumor-suppressing anti-ENG monoclonal TRC105.
evidence.explanation: Crystallography places HHT1-mutated residues directly on the BMP9-binding surface of endoglin, which is the structural reason ENG variants impair this pathway and not merely a correlation between the two.

evidence.snippet: The structure of the C-terminal zona pellucida module suggests how two copies of ENG embrace homodimeric BMP9, whose binding is compatible with ligand recognition by type I but not type II receptors.
evidence.explanation: Explains endoglin's ligand-presentation role to the type I receptor ALK1, which is the architecture this node depends on.

steps/4.description: Endoglin acts as a co-receptor alongside ALK1, the ACVRL1 gene product, in the endothelial BMP9 pathway that phosphorylates SMAD1/5/8. Reduced endoglin lowers signalling through this axis. That ENG and ACVRL1 lesions converge on one pathway is the accepted explanation for why HHT1 and HHT2 are clinically similar disorders despite different genes.

evidence.snippet: The primitive vascular plexus of the yolk sac fails to mature into defined vessels, and vascular channels dilate and rupture.
evidence.explanation: Shows that removing endoglin leaves vessel maturation disordered and the resulting channels fragile.

evidence.snippet: Mutations in these genes lead to an underproduction of functional proteins, resulting in excessive abnormal angiogenesis [10].
evidence.explanation: States the angiogenic consequence of underproduced ENG/ACVRL1 protein.

steps/5.description: Endothelial cells deficient in endoglin signalling mount a disordered angiogenic and remodelling response. In the endoglin-null embryo the primitive vascular plexus fails to mature into defined vessels and the resulting channels dilate and rupture, which is the developmental extreme of the same defect.

evidence.snippet: Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia (HHT) is characterized by the presence of multiple arteriovenous malformations (AVMs) that lack intervening capillaries and result in direct connections between arteries and veins.
evidence.explanation: Defines the architectural lesion this node names.

evidence.snippet: Large AVMs occur most often in the lungs, liver, or brain; complications from bleeding or shunting may be sudden and catastrophic.
evidence.explanation: Supports the branch of this node into the organ-specific lesions below it.

steps/6.description: The defining lesion of HHT is an arteriovenous malformation that lacks intervening capillaries, so an artery drains directly into a vein. Small lesions of this kind are the mucocutaneous telangiectases; large ones are the visceral AVMs. Both the fragility that causes bleeding and the shunt physiology that causes the neurological complications follow from this single architectural change.

evidence.snippet: Telangiectases (small AVMs) are characteristically found on the lips, tongue, buccal and gastrointestinal (GI) mucosa, fingers, and nose.
evidence.explanation: Establishes that telangiectases are small AVMs and gives their characteristic distribution.

evidence.snippet: Six of fifteen (40%) nasal and two of four (50%) dermal telangiectasia had a detectable somatic second hit.
evidence.explanation: Links these specific lesions back to the second-hit node upstream.

steps/7.description: Small AVMs form in the nasal, oral and gastrointestinal mucosa and in the skin of the fingers and face. These thin-walled lesions bleed on minor trauma, which makes them the source of epistaxis and of chronic occult gastrointestinal blood loss. Somatic second hits are detectable in a substantial fraction of nasal and dermal telangiectases.

evidence.snippet: PAVMs and CAVMs were significantly more frequent in HHT1 (75% vs. 44%, P < 0.0005; 20% vs. 0%, P < 0.002, respectively) and HAVMs in HHT2 (60% vs. 84%, P < 0.01).
evidence.explanation: The core HHT1-versus-HHT2 contrast: pulmonary and cerebral AVMs are the HHT1 pattern, hepatic AVMs the HHT2 pattern.

evidence.snippet: Symptomatic PAVMs were more frequent in HHT1 (34.4 vs. 5.2%, P<0.001), as were cerebral abscesses (7.5 vs. 0.8%, P=0.002).
evidence.explanation: Independent replication of the PAVM excess in HHT1 in a separate national cohort, using symptomatic rather than screen-detected lesions.

evidence.snippet: The prevalence of pulmonary arteriovenous malformations (AVM) is higher in HHT type 1, whereas hepatic AVMs are more common in HHT2.
evidence.explanation: A third independent cohort reporting the same directional contrast.

steps/8.description: Pulmonary AVMs are the signature visceral lesion of HHT1 and are markedly more frequent here than in ACVRL1-related HHT2. They were found in 75% of HHT1 versus 44% of HHT2 patients on systematic imaging in one series, and symptomatic PAVMs in 34.4% of HHT1 versus 5.2% of HHT2 in a second. Because they bypass the pulmonary capillary filter, they create a right-to-left shunt rather than acting only as a bleeding source.

evidence.snippet: HHT1 is more frequently associated with congenital AVM malformations, such as CAVMs and PAVMs whereas HHT2 predominantly involves the liver.
evidence.explanation: States the cerebral and pulmonary predilection of HHT1 as the authors' conclusion.

evidence.snippet: including the loss of heterozygosity in ENG in one brain AVM sample, in which the germline mutation occurred in a different allele than a nearby somatic mutation (both are loss-of-function mutations)
evidence.explanation: Anchors the cerebral lesion to demonstrated biallelic ENG loss.

steps/9.description: Cerebral AVMs are the second lesion that distinguishes HHT1. In one systematic series they were present in 20% of HHT1 patients and in none of the HHT2 patients screened. A brain AVM is also the lesion in which biallelic ENG inactivation has been demonstrated directly.

evidence.snippet: Neurological manifestations secondary to CAVMs/PAVMs were found only in HHT1 patients, whereas severe liver involvement was detected only in HHT2.
evidence.explanation: Attributes the neurological consequences specifically to the shunting lesions and specifically to HHT1.

evidence.snippet: Respiratory symptoms were mainly detected in HHT1.
evidence.explanation: Supports the respiratory limb of this node as an HHT1-predominant finding.

evidence.snippet: When pulmonary shunting is present, use antibiotic prophylaxis for dental and non-sterile invasive procedures, taking care to prevent air bubbles from being introduced in intravenous lines
evidence.explanation: The prophylaxis recommendation exists because the shunt carries bacteria and air past the pulmonary filter, which is the mechanism this node states.

steps/10.description: Blood traversing a pulmonary AVM bypasses both gas exchange and the pulmonary capillary filter. The first consequence is hypoxemia and exertional breathlessness; the second is that venous emboli and bacteria reach the systemic and cerebral circulation, producing paradoxical embolic stroke and brain abscess. Neurological manifestations secondary to shunting were observed only in HHT1 patients in a systematically screened cohort, and respiratory symptoms were likewise mainly an HHT1 finding.

evidence.snippet: The most common clinical manifestation is recurrent nosebleeds (epistaxis) beginning on average at age 12 years.
evidence.explanation: Establishes epistaxis as the commonest manifestation and gives the typical age of onset.

evidence.snippet: Epistaxis debuts earlier and may be more severe in HHT1 than in HHT2.
evidence.explanation: Supplies the HHT1-specific onset and severity contrast that makes this phenotype subtype-discriminating rather than generic.

evidence.snippet: Epistaxis occurred later in HHT2, with incomplete penetrance (P<0.0001).
evidence.explanation: Independent cohort reporting the same direction of effect, expressed as later onset in HHT2.

steps/11.description: Spontaneous recurrent nosebleeds from nasal mucosal telangiectases are the usual presenting feature, beginning on average at age 12 years. Onset is earlier and severity greater in HHT1 than in ACVRL1-related HHT2.

evidence.snippet: Telangiectases (small AVMs) are characteristically found on the lips, tongue, buccal and gastrointestinal (GI) mucosa, fingers, and nose.
evidence.explanation: Gives the characteristic anatomical distribution used diagnostically.

evidence.snippet: The appearance of telangiectases is generally later than epistaxis but may be during childhood.
evidence.explanation: Supports the described timing relative to epistaxis.

steps/12.description: Characteristic small AVMs of the lips, tongue, buccal and gastrointestinal mucosa, fingers and nose. Their appearance is generally later than epistaxis but may occur during childhood.

evidence.snippet: PAVMs and CAVMs were significantly more frequent in HHT1 (75% vs. 44%, P < 0.0005; 20% vs. 0%, P < 0.002, respectively) and HAVMs in HHT2 (60% vs. 84%, P < 0.01).
evidence.explanation: Gives the HHT1 frequency (75%) that this record's FREQUENT band is drawn from, alongside the HHT2 comparison.

evidence.snippet: PAVMs were more frequently detected in asymptomatic HHT1 patients (54 vs. 12.8%, P<0.0001).
evidence.explanation: Supports the statement that much of the HHT1 PAVM burden is clinically silent and only found by screening.

evidence.snippet: The ENG gene should be first targeted for mutational screening in the presence of large PAVM in patients < 45 years.
evidence.explanation: The authors' clinical corollary: a large PAVM makes ENG the first gene to test, which is the practical expression of this genotype-phenotype link.

steps/13.description: The HHT1-defining visceral lesion. Detected in 75% of HHT1 versus 44% of HHT2 patients on systematic screening, and symptomatic in 34.4% of HHT1 versus 5.2% of HHT2 in an independent cohort. Frequently clinically silent, so the excess in HHT1 is even larger among screen-detected than among symptomatic lesions, which is why screening rather than symptom-led investigation is the standard of care.

evidence.snippet: PAVMs and CAVMs were significantly more frequent in HHT1 (75% vs. 44%, P < 0.0005; 20% vs. 0%, P < 0.002, respectively) and HAVMs in HHT2 (60% vs. 84%, P < 0.01).
evidence.explanation: Gives the 20% HHT1 cerebral AVM frequency behind the OCCASIONAL band, and the 0% HHT2 comparison.

steps/14.description: Present in 20% of HHT1 patients and in none of the HHT2 patients in a systematically screened series. Cerebral AVMs may bleed, and are managed by surgery, embolotherapy or stereotactic radiosurgery according to size, location and symptoms.

evidence.snippet: Symptomatic PAVMs were more frequent in HHT1 (34.4 vs. 5.2%, P<0.001), as were cerebral abscesses (7.5 vs. 0.8%, P=0.002).
evidence.explanation: Gives the HHT1 cerebral abscess frequency and its excess over HHT2, in the same sentence that reports the PAVM excess that causes it.

steps/15.description: A consequence of loss of the pulmonary capillary filter rather than of a cerebral lesion. Cerebral abscesses occurred in 7.5% of HHT1 versus 0.8% of HHT2 patients.

evidence.snippet: Pulmonary AVMs with a feeding vessel 2-3 mm or greater in diameter typically require occlusion for stroke prevention.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the PAVM-stroke link as the basis of a standard intervention.

evidence.snippet: Nearly one in five patients in our HHT population has been diagnosed with stroke or cerebral abscess, indicating a high prevalence of cerebral complications.
evidence.explanation: Quantifies the cerebral complication burden. Indirect because the figure pools stroke with cerebral abscess and covers the cohort's mixed genotypes, not HHT1 alone; no frequency band is assigned to this record as a result.

steps/16.description: Paradoxical embolism through a pulmonary AVM. Occlusion of PAVMs with a feeding vessel of 2-3 mm or greater is performed specifically for stroke prevention. Nearly one in five patients in an unselected HHT cohort had been diagnosed with stroke or cerebral abscess.

evidence.snippet: Respiratory symptoms were mainly detected in HHT1.
evidence.explanation: Supports respiratory involvement as HHT1-predominant. Indirect because the quote names respiratory symptoms generally rather than measured hypoxemia.

steps/17.description: Blood shunted through a pulmonary AVM bypasses gas exchange, producing hypoxemia and exertional breathlessness. Respiratory symptoms were mainly an HHT1 finding in a systematically screened cohort.

evidence.snippet: Gastrointestinal bleeding occurred more frequently in HHT2 (16.4 vs. 6.5%, P=0.017).
evidence.explanation: Gives the HHT1 frequency (6.5%) behind the OCCASIONAL band and records that this manifestation runs opposite to the pulmonary/cerebral pattern.

evidence.snippet: Some individuals with HHT have GI bleeding, which is rarely seen before age 50 years.
evidence.explanation: Supports the late age of onset stated in the description.

steps/18.description: Bleeding from gastrointestinal mucosal telangiectases, rarely seen before age 50 years. Unlike the pulmonary and cerebral lesions, this is the one major manifestation reported as less frequent in HHT1 than in HHT2 (6.5% versus 16.4%).

evidence.snippet: GI bleeding and anemia is treated with iron replacement therapy and (if needed) blood transfusions.
evidence.explanation: Establishes anemia as a managed complication of the bleeding phenotype.

evidence.snippet: Annual evaluation by a health care provider familiar with HHT for signs and symptoms of complications; annual hematocrit, hemoglobin, and ferritin
evidence.explanation: The recommended surveillance is iron-status monitoring, which reflects iron deficiency as the expected hematological consequence.

steps/19.description: Chronic blood loss from epistaxis and gastrointestinal telangiectases produces iron deficiency, managed with iron replacement and, when necessary, transfusion. Annual hematocrit, hemoglobin and ferritin monitoring is recommended.

evidence.snippet: PAVMs and CAVMs were significantly more frequent in HHT1 (75% vs. 44%, P < 0.0005; 20% vs. 0%, P < 0.002, respectively) and HAVMs in HHT2 (60% vs. 84%, P < 0.01).
evidence.explanation: Gives the HHT1 hepatic AVM frequency (60%) behind the FREQUENT band and records that it is significantly lower than in HHT2.

evidence.snippet: Neurological manifestations secondary to CAVMs/PAVMs were found only in HHT1 patients, whereas severe liver involvement was detected only in HHT2.
evidence.explanation: Refutes any claim that severe or symptomatic hepatic disease is an HHT1 manifestation: in this cohort it occurred only in HHT2.

steps/20.description: Hepatic AVMs do occur in HHT1 - 60% on systematic imaging in one series - but they are the HHT2-predominant lesion (84% there), and symptomatic hepatic involvement was seen only in HHT2 patients in two independent cohorts. This record is curated to prevent the common error of reading the HHT2 hepatic pattern as an HHT1 feature.

evidence.snippet: Congestive heart failure (69%, 95% CI: 56-80%) and pulmonary hypertension (23%, 95% CI: 14-36%) were the main non-fatal comorbidities in patients with HHT.
evidence.explanation: Quantifies congestive heart failure as the leading non-fatal comorbidity.

evidence.snippet: Symptomatic hepatic AVMs are managed medically; liver transplantation is recommended for individuals who do not respond to medical therapy and who develop refractory high-output heart failure.
evidence.explanation: Ties the high-output failure explicitly to hepatic AVMs and gives the escalation pathway.

steps/21.description: High-output cardiac failure driven by hepatic arteriovenous shunting. It was the commonest non-fatal comorbidity in a cohort of deceased HHT patients (69%) and the second commonest cause of death (26%). Symptomatic hepatic AVMs are managed medically, with liver transplantation reserved for refractory high-output failure. Because the hepatic lesion burden is greater in HHT2, this is not an HHT1-predominant manifestation, but it does occur in HHT1 and is the mechanism connecting the hepatic lesion to mortality.

evidence.snippet: Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia type 1 (HHT1) is associated with mutations in the Endoglin gene, leading to haploinsufficiency.
evidence.explanation: States the step from ENG mutation to haploinsufficiency, which is exactly this edge.

edges/1.description: Only the wild-type allele produces surface protein, so the germline truncating allele translates directly into reduced endothelial endoglin.

evidence.snippet: We also demonstrate, using siRNA depletion of ENG and novel anti-ENG antibodies, that ENG is required for BMP9/pSMAD1 signaling in all human and mouse endothelial cells tested.
evidence.explanation: Depleting ENG abolishes BMP9/pSMAD1 signaling, which establishes the dependence this edge asserts.

edges/2.description: Endoglin is required for BMP9-driven SMAD1 phosphorylation in endothelial cells, so reduced endoglin lowers flux through this pathway.

evidence.snippet: Finally, anti-ENG antibodies that interfere with BMP9/pSMAD1 signaling, but not with TGFβ1/pSMAD3 signaling, also decrease in vitro HUVEC endothelial tube formation
evidence.explanation: Blocking the BMP9/pSMAD1 arm alone changes endothelial tube formation, tying this signalling deficit to an altered angiogenic response.

edges/3.description: Loss of BMP9/ALK1/endoglin signalling releases the endothelium from a pathway required for orderly angiogenesis.

evidence.snippet: This is the first report that nasal telangiectasias and solid organ AVMs in HHT are caused by very-low-level somatic biallelic second-hit mutations.
evidence.explanation: States the causal claim this edge makes, that the second hit is what produces the lesion.

edges/4.description: Biallelic inactivation in a clone of endothelial cells converts a uniformly haploinsufficient vasculature into a focal lesion.

evidence.snippet: Large AVMs occur most often in the lungs, liver, or brain; complications from bleeding or shunting may be sudden and catastrophic.
evidence.explanation: Names the liver among the organs in which the capillary-free AVM lesion forms.

edges/9.description: Hepatic AVMs arise by the same architectural mechanism in HHT1, though they are the lesion that predominates in HHT2 rather than here.

evidence.snippet: Pulmonary AVMs with a feeding vessel 2-3 mm or greater in diameter typically require occlusion for stroke prevention.
evidence.explanation: Occluding the PAVM is done to prevent stroke, which is only coherent if the PAVM is the conduit for the shunt this edge asserts.

edges/13.description: A pulmonary AVM connects pulmonary artery to pulmonary vein without an intervening capillary bed, which is what constitutes the shunt.

evidence.snippet: When pulmonary shunting is present, use antibiotic prophylaxis for dental and non-sterile invasive procedures, taking care to prevent air bubbles from being introduced in intravenous lines
evidence.explanation: Prophylaxis is conditioned specifically on the presence of shunting, which is the causal step this edge asserts. Indirect because it states a preventive measure rather than reporting abscess incidence.

edges/17.description: Bacteria that would normally be cleared by the pulmonary capillary bed reach the systemic and cerebral circulation through the shunt.

evidence.snippet: Pulmonary AVMs with a feeding vessel 2-3 mm or greater in diameter typically require occlusion for stroke prevention.
evidence.explanation: Closing the shunt is done to prevent stroke, which asserts the causal direction of this edge rather than mere co-occurrence.

edges/18.description: Venous emboli bypass the pulmonary filter and enter the systemic circulation, producing paradoxical embolic stroke.

evidence.snippet: GI bleeding and anemia is treated with iron replacement therapy and (if needed) blood transfusions.
evidence.explanation: Treating the anemia with iron replacement presupposes that the bleeding causes iron deficiency, which is the edge asserted here.

edges/19.description: Chronic blood loss from this site depletes iron stores.

evidence.snippet: GI bleeding and anemia is treated with iron replacement therapy and (if needed) blood transfusions.
evidence.explanation: Treating the anemia with iron replacement presupposes that the bleeding causes iron deficiency, which is the edge asserted here.

edges/20.description: Chronic blood loss from this site depletes iron stores.

evidence.snippet: Symptomatic hepatic AVMs are managed medically; liver transplantation is recommended for individuals who do not respond to medical therapy and who develop refractory high-output heart failure.
evidence.explanation: Names high-output heart failure as the consequence of the hepatic lesion that drives escalation to transplantation.

edges/21.description: Hepatic arteriovenous shunting raises cardiac output and can drive high-output cardiac failure.

evidence.snippet: We have identified endoglin as the HHT gene mapping to 9q3 and have established HHT as the first human disease defined by a mutation in a member of the TGF-beta receptor complex.
evidence.explanation: The gene-identification result that defines HHT1 as the ENG-related form.

evidence.snippet: We have identified mutations in three affected individuals: a C to G substitution converting a tyrosine to a termination codon, a 39 base pair deletion and a 2 basepair deletion which creates a premature termination codon.
evidence.explanation: The founding allele series is truncating, which is the basis for assigning functional_impact_category LOSS_OF_FUNCTION.

evidence.snippet: Endoglin (ENG), activin A receptor type II-like 1 (ACVRL1/ALK1), and SMAD4 mutations cause HHT1 (OMIM 187300), HHT2 (OMIM 600376), and the combined Juvenile Polyposis/HHT (JP/HHT) syndrome (OMIM 175050), respectively [3,4,5].
evidence.explanation: Confirms the gene-to-numbered-type assignment, including the OMIM anchor 187300 for the ENG form curated here.

genes/0.notes: Heterozygous loss-of-function variants in ENG at 9q34, encoding the endothelial TGF-beta superfamily co-receptor endoglin, define HHT1. The originally reported alleles were a nonsense substitution and two deletions creating premature termination codons, establishing a truncating, loss-of-function mechanism from the outset.

evidence.snippet: Pulmonary AVMs with a feeding vessel 2-3 mm or greater in diameter typically require occlusion for stroke prevention.
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews gives the size threshold and the indication for occlusion.

treatments/0.description: Transcatheter occlusion of pulmonary AVMs with a feeding vessel 2-3 mm or greater in diameter, performed to prevent paradoxical embolic stroke rather than to treat symptoms. Because PAVMs are both more frequent and more often asymptomatic in HHT1, this is the intervention most specific to this genotype.

evidence.snippet: Pulmonary AVMs with a feeding vessel 2-3 mm or greater in diameter typically require occlusion for stroke prevention.
evidence.explanation: States both the intervention and the shunt-mediated complication it is aimed at.

treatments/0/targets/0.description: Occluding the feeding artery closes the conduit that carries emboli and bacteria past the pulmonary capillary filter.

evidence.snippet: When pulmonary shunting is present, use antibiotic prophylaxis for dental and non-sterile invasive procedures, taking care to prevent air bubbles from being introduced in intravenous lines
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews management recommendation for shunt-associated infection risk.

treatments/1.description: Antibiotic prophylaxis before dental and non-sterile invasive procedures in patients with pulmonary shunting, together with care to exclude air bubbles from intravenous lines. Both measures address the loss of the pulmonary filter rather than the vascular lesion itself.

evidence.snippet: When pulmonary shunting is present, use antibiotic prophylaxis for dental and non-sterile invasive procedures, taking care to prevent air bubbles from being introduced in intravenous lines
evidence.explanation: Conditions the recommendation explicitly on the presence of pulmonary shunting, which is the mechanism targeted.

treatments/1/targets/0.description: Prophylaxis and air-bubble precautions counter the passage of bacteria and air emboli through the shunt to the systemic circulation.

evidence.snippet: At 24 weeks, the mean difference between the pomalidomide group and the placebo group in the change from baseline in the Epistaxis Severity Score was -0.94 points (95% confidence interval [CI], -1.57 to -0.31; P = 0.004).
evidence.explanation: The primary efficacy result behind this treatment record.

evidence.snippet: Adverse events that were more common in the pomalidomide group than in the placebo group included neutropenia, constipation, and rash.
evidence.explanation: Records the toxicity profile stated in the description.

treatments/2.description: An immunomodulatory antiangiogenic agent. In the randomized, placebo-controlled PATH-HHT trial (NCT03910244), pomalidomide reduced Epistaxis Severity Score at 24 weeks by a mean of 0.94 points more than placebo; the trial was stopped early at a planned interim analysis for efficacy. Neutropenia, constipation and rash were more common on pomalidomide. The trial enrolled HHT patients without restricting to ENG genotype.

evidence.snippet: Among patients with HHT, pomalidomide treatment resulted in a significant, clinically relevant reduction in epistaxis severity.
evidence.explanation: Indirect: the trial measured epistaxis severity, a clinical readout, and did not image or biopsy the telangiectases themselves.

treatments/2/targets/0.description: Reducing epistaxis severity implies action on the nasal mucosal telangiectases that bleed.

evidence.snippet: Targeted therapies: Oral tranexamic acid or intravenous bevacizumab for epistaxis and GI bleeding; pomalidomide or pazopanib for refractory epistaxis and GI bleeding.
evidence.explanation: Places tranexamic acid among the recommended targeted therapies for the bleeding phenotype.

treatments/3.description: Oral antifibrinolytic therapy, listed by GeneReviews as a targeted therapy for epistaxis and gastrointestinal bleeding in HHT.

evidence.snippet: Targeted therapies: Oral tranexamic acid or intravenous bevacizumab for epistaxis and GI bleeding; pomalidomide or pazopanib for refractory epistaxis and GI bleeding.
evidence.explanation: Lists bevacizumab among the recommended targeted therapies.

treatments/4.description: Intravenous anti-VEGF monoclonal antibody used for epistaxis and gastrointestinal bleeding, and in symptomatic hepatic AVM disease. Its rationale is antiangiogenic, acting on the dysregulated angiogenic response downstream of impaired endoglin signalling.

evidence.snippet: Mutations in these genes lead to an underproduction of functional proteins, resulting in excessive abnormal angiogenesis [10].
evidence.explanation: Indirect: it establishes the angiogenic target that antiangiogenic therapy is aimed at, rather than reporting the drug's effect.

treatments/4/targets/0.description: VEGF blockade opposes the excessive abnormal angiogenesis that follows underproduction of endoglin.

evidence.snippet: GI bleeding and anemia is treated with iron replacement therapy and (if needed) blood transfusions.
evidence.explanation: States the treatment pathway for the anemia phenotype.

treatments/5.description: Iron replacement therapy for the iron deficiency anemia caused by chronic blood loss, with red cell transfusion when anemia is symptomatic despite aggressive iron replacement.

evidence.snippet: Cerebral AVMs are treated as indicated by size, location, or symptoms by surgery, embolotherapy, and/or stereotactic radiosurgery.
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews management recommendation for cerebral AVMs.

treatments/6.description: Cerebral AVMs are treated according to size, location or symptoms by surgery, embolotherapy and/or stereotactic radiosurgery.

evidence.snippet: Cerebral AVMs are treated as indicated by size, location, or symptoms by surgery, embolotherapy, and/or stereotactic radiosurgery.
evidence.explanation: Names the lesion targeted and the modalities used against it.

treatments/6/targets/0.description: These modalities obliterate the cerebral lesion itself.

evidence.snippet: Molecular genetic testing should be offered to at-risk family members if the germline pathogenic variant has been identified in the family.
evidence.explanation: States the cascade-testing recommendation this record covers.

evidence.snippet: Each child of an individual with HHT has a 50% chance of inheriting the pathogenic variant.
evidence.explanation: Gives the recurrence risk that counseling conveys.

treatments/7.description: Autosomal dominant transmission with a 50% recurrence risk to offspring makes counseling and cascade testing central to management. Once the family variant is known, predictive testing of at-risk relatives is possible; if it is not, at-risk relatives are screened clinically.

evidence.snippet: Agents/circumstances to avoid: Vigorous nose blowing; lifting heavy objects; straining during bowel movements; finger manipulation in the nose; anticoagulant and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory agents that interfere with clotting (including aspirin) should be avoided in individuals with significant nose or GI bleeding unless required for treatment of other medical condition; scuba diving unless TCE within the last five years was negative for evidence of a right-to-left shunt; liver biopsy.
evidence.explanation: The GeneReviews drug-safety and circumstance warnings quoted verbatim.

treatments/8.description: GeneReviews lists agents and circumstances to avoid in HHT. Anticoagulant and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory agents that interfere with clotting, including aspirin, should be avoided where nose or GI bleeding is significant unless required for another condition. Vigorous nose blowing, heavy lifting, straining at stool and nasal finger manipulation are avoided because they provoke bleeding from mucosal telangiectases. Scuba diving is avoided unless contrast echocardiography within five years excluded a right-to-left shunt, and liver biopsy is avoided. The diving and biopsy restrictions bear particularly on HHT1, where pulmonary shunting is the predominant lesion.

evidence.snippet: Patients with HHT harbor these heterozygous germline mutations in every cell of the body, yet vascular malformations occur in only a small minority of vessels, with predilection for specific anatomic locations.
evidence.explanation: States the anatomical predilection as an open observation rather than an explained one.

open_questions/0.rationale: The second-hit model explains why lesions are focal, but not why HHT1 lesions favour lung and brain while ACVRL1-related HHT2 lesions favour liver. Both genes act in the same BMP9/ALK1/SMAD pathway, and second hits have now been demonstrated in both. The organ preference is therefore unexplained by the pathway model and by the second-hit model taken together, and no tissue-level determinant - flow environment, endothelial subtype, local BMP9 availability - has been established as the discriminating factor.

evidence.snippet: In this murine model of HHT, it appears that epigenetic factors and modifier genes, some of which are present in 129/Ola, contribute to disease heterogeneity.
evidence.explanation: Establishes that modifiers exist and are unidentified, which is the gap.

evidence.snippet: The severity of epistaxis and number and location of telangiectases and AVMs vary significantly, even among affected individuals from the same family who have the same genetic mutation [7].
evidence.explanation: The human counterpart of the mouse observation, stating within-family variability at identical genotype.

open_questions/1.rationale: Severity of epistaxis and the number and location of lesions vary markedly even within a family sharing one ENG variant, and the Eng+/- mouse shows the same effect as a strain-background dependence, which is direct evidence that modifiers exist. The mouse work names 129/Ola as a permissive background but does not identify the responsible loci, and no human modifier has been established. Resolving this would matter clinically because it is the variability, not the genotype, that currently limits prediction of who will develop a pulmonary or cerebral AVM.

evidence.snippet: A total of 159 patients will be randomized 2:1 to treatment with oral pomalidomide or matching placebo for 24 weeks.
evidence.explanation: The registered design specifies randomization without genotype stratification, which is the basis of this gap.

open_questions/2.rationale: Every systemic therapy curated here was trialled in HHT patients selected by clinical diagnosis rather than by genotype. PATH-HHT enrolled on epistaxis severity and transfusion dependence and reports no ENG-versus-ACVRL1 subgroup. Since the two genotypes differ substantially in which organs are affected, a genotype-stratified analysis is a reasonable expectation that the literature does not yet supply, and treatment records in this entry should not be read as HHT1-specific efficacy claims.

evidence.snippet: In contrast, the TS mutants form inclusion bodies, a strong indication that they are misfolded (Supplementary Fig. 2).
evidence.explanation: Direct biophysical evidence that the variants destabilise the domain's fold.

evidence.snippet: All mutations are within the targeting-sequence domain of DNMT1.
evidence.explanation: Establishes that the causal variants are confined to this one domain.

evidence.snippet: Strikingly, all causative mutations described to date affect a genomic region in DNMT1, which codes for the TS domain
evidence.explanation: Independent confirmation that the mutational spectrum is restricted to this domain.

evidence.snippet: The RFTS domain directly associates with the methyltransferase domain, thereby inhibiting the substrate binding of hDNMT1.
evidence.explanation: Structural evidence that the domain the variants destabilise is not only a targeting module but an autoinhibitory one, which is why a misfold there disturbs catalysis without touching the active site.

evidence.snippet: Five novel mutations of DNMT1 were discovered; p.C353F, p.T481P, p.P491L, p.Y524D and p.I531N, all within the target-sequence domain, and two mutations (p.T481P, p.P491L) arising de novo.
evidence.explanation: Five further alleles, all in the same domain, and the first de novo cases - which matter because they establish the variants as causal independently of segregation.

steps/1.description: The initiating lesion. Causal variants cluster in the targeting sequence (TS, also RFTS) domain encoded by exons 20 and 21, and the residues involved sit in the hydrophobic core or the linker between the domain's two subdomains rather than at the catalytic site. Expressed in bacteria, wild-type TS domain is soluble while the mutant domains form inclusion bodies - direct evidence of misfolding rather than of an altered but folded protein.

evidence.snippet: With cell-based assays, we could show that HSANIE associated mutations perturb DNMT1 heterochromatin association and catalytic complex formation at methylation sites and decrease protein stability in late S and G2 phase.
evidence.explanation: Names all three components of this node and the cell-cycle phase in which the instability appears.

evidence.snippet: The mutant DNMT1 protein shows premature degradation and reduced DNA methyltransferase activity.
evidence.explanation: Independent statement of the stability and activity defect.

steps/2.description: Three consequences of the same misfold, which is why they are one node rather than three. The protein is degraded in late S and G2 phase; it fails to remain associated with heterochromatin when it should; and it loses the UHRF1 interaction that normally delivers it to hemimethylated substrate after replication. The enzyme's catalytic domain is intact, so this is a failure of delivery and persistence rather than of chemistry - which is why measured methyltransferase activity falls without the active site being touched.

evidence.snippet: In the 3 affected siblings, overall methylation loss was consistently found in all chromosomes with X and 18 being most affected.
evidence.explanation: The genome-wide hypomethylation result in patient germline DNA.

evidence.snippet: In some CpG islands, hypermethylated CpGs outnumbered hypomethylated CpGs. In 201 imprinted genes, there were more DMCs than in non-imprinted genes and most were hypomethylated.
evidence.explanation: The site-specific hypermethylation and the imprinted-gene excess, which are what make this node a redistribution rather than a simple deficit.

evidence.snippet: Differentially methylated region (DMR) analysis identified 5649 hypomethylated and 1872 hypermethylated regions.
evidence.explanation: Quantifies the two directions of change at region level.

steps/3.description: The epigenomic phenotype, and the reason this disease is not simply "loss of methylation". Whole-genome bisulfite sequencing of three patient-sibling pairs found consistent methylation loss across all chromosomes, with X and chromosome 18 most affected, and over half a million differentially methylated CpG sites. Hypomethylation predominates in promoters, exons, most CpG islands and repeat classes - but within some CpG islands hypermethylated sites outnumber hypomethylated ones, and imprinted genes carry more differentially methylated sites than non-imprinted genes. A maintenance enzyme that is mistargeted rather than simply absent produces exactly this mixed picture.

evidence.snippet: Despite its well-known replication-coupled function as maintenance DNA methyltransferase in proliferating cells, DNMT1 is highly expressed in embryonic and adult postmitotic neurons, especially in the central nervous system (CNS)
evidence.explanation: The expression fact that makes a postmitotic neuronal phenotype possible at all for a replication-coupled enzyme.

steps/4.description: The cellular consequence. DNMT1 is highly expressed in postmitotic neurons despite its canonical role being replication-coupled, which is the standing puzzle of this disease: how a maintenance methyltransferase defect damages cells that are not dividing.
