Cells expressing mutant DNMT1 are apoptosis-prone and fail to enter the neuronal lineage in differentiation assays.

evidence.snippet: Quantitative sensory testing, nerve conductions, and nerve biopsy were indicative of length dependent progressive sensory axonal loss.
evidence.explanation: Three independent modalities converging on the same pathological description.

evidence.snippet: Electrophysiological studies revealed absent sensory nerve action potential with nearly normal motor nerve conduction studies.
evidence.explanation: The electrophysiological dissociation that establishes the selectivity for sensory fibres.

steps/5.description: The peripheral arm. Quantitative sensory testing, nerve conduction studies and nerve biopsy all indicate progressive sensory axonal loss in a length-dependent distribution, with nerve pathology showing axonal loss without inflammatory or infiltrative inclusions. Sensory nerve action potentials are absent while motor conduction is near-normal, which is what makes this a pure sensory neuropathy rather than a sensorimotor one.

evidence.snippet: Brain imaging of affected persons showed global atrophy and reduced weight of autopsied brains.
evidence.explanation: Imaging and post-mortem evidence of central neurodegeneration.

evidence.snippet: Pathologic studies of affected persons' nerve7, brain14 and spinal cord (Fig. 1) show axonal loss without interstitial infiltrative inclusions.
evidence.explanation: Establishes that the lesion is axonal loss rather than an inclusion pathology. The snippet carries the source's inline reference markers, quoted as written.

steps/6.description: The central arm. Brain imaging shows global atrophy and autopsied brains are reduced in weight; functional imaging in one kindred suggested medial frontal and thalamic hypometabolism. As in the nerve, the pathology is axonal loss without infiltrative inclusions, so this is not a proteinopathy.

evidence.snippet: These mutations cause premature degradation of mutant proteins, reduced methyltransferase activity and impaired heterochromatin binding during the G2 cell cycle phase leading to global hypomethylation and site-specific hypermethylation.
evidence.explanation: The founding paper's own causal chain, from the variant through protein stability and chromatin binding to the methylation phenotype.

edges/1.description: A misfolded domain is both unstable and unable to perform the binding the domain exists for, so the misfolding produces the degradation and the targeting failure together.

evidence.snippet: we showed that DNMT1 mutations P496Y and Y500C identified in HSANIE patients not only impair DNMT1 heterochromatin association, but also UHRF1 interaction resulting in hypomethylation.
evidence.explanation: Traces the specific molecular failures - chromatin association and UHRF1 binding - through to the methylation outcome.

edges/2.description: An enzyme that is not delivered to its substrate and does not persist through the cell cycle cannot maintain the methylation pattern across replication.

evidence.snippet: To investigate the neuronal phenotype of HSANIE mutations, we performed DNMT1 rescue assays and could show that cells expressing mutated DNMT1 were prone to apoptosis and failed to differentiate into neuronal lineage.
evidence.explanation: The cellular consequence, demonstrated in a rescue assay so the effect is attributable to the mutant protein rather than to the assay background.

edges/3.description: Cells expressing mutant DNMT1 die and fail to become neurons. Which of the thousands of differentially methylated regions mediates this is not established, so the intermediates are recorded as unknown.

edges/4.description: Sensory neurons are among the cell types lost. Why the loss is length-dependent and why sensory neurons are affected before motor neurons is not established.

edges/5.description: The same cellular vulnerability in the central nervous system, producing the global atrophy seen on imaging and at autopsy.

evidence.snippet: Exome sequencing led to the identification of DNMT1 mutation c.1484A>G (p.Tyr495Cys) in two American kindreds and one Japanese kindred and a triple nucleotide change, c.1470-1472TCC>ATA (p.Asp490Glu-Pro491Tyr), in one European kindred.
evidence.explanation: Establishes DNMT1 as causal and names the founding alleles.

evidence.snippet: Asp490 is solvent accessible (ASA is 75.3 Å2) and is therefore unlikely to contribute to the disease phenotype (Fig. 2f).
evidence.explanation: The structural argument that dissects which half of the double substitution matters.

evidence.snippet: Using a next-generation sequencing system, 16 candidate genes were analyzed and a novel missense mutation, c.1706A>G (p.His569Arg), was identified in exon 21 of DNMT1.
evidence.explanation: The exon 21 allele producing an HSAN phenotype.

genes/0.notes: All reported causal variants lie in exons 20 and 21, encoding the targeting sequence (replication focus targeting sequence) domain. Reported alleles include c.1484A>G (p.Tyr495Cys) in American and Japanese kindreds, the triple-nucleotide change c.1470-1472TCC>ATA (p.Asp490Glu-Pro491Tyr) in a European kindred, a novel p.Tyr495His, and c.1706A>G (p.His569Arg) in exon 21 in a sporadic Japanese case. Structural analysis of the founding variants indicates that Tyr495 sits in the hydrophobic core while Asp490 is solvent-accessible and unlikely to contribute, so within the p.Asp490Glu-Pro491Tyr allele the Pro491 change is the likely driver.

evidence.snippet: The emphasis of management is to help affected individuals and their caregivers understand the sudomotor defect and injury prevention when sensory impairment is significant.
evidence.explanation: The GeneReviews management statement, naming injury prevention as the emphasis.

evidence.snippet: Examination of feet daily for evidence of skin injury; annual routine clinical testing for dementia and audiogram to monitor hearing loss.
evidence.explanation: The full GeneReviews surveillance recommendation. The daily foot inspection is what this treatment is; the annual dementia and audiogram testing is recorded here too because the three are one recommendation in the source.

treatments/0.description: There is no disease-modifying therapy. The intervention with the clearest mechanistic rationale is preventing the injury the patient cannot feel: daily foot inspection, protective socks and shoes, and avoiding exposures that would injure skin with reduced sensation. This targets the downstream complication - infection and amputation - rather than the neuropathy.

treatments/0/targets/0.description: Protection does not slow the degeneration; it prevents the injury that the degeneration makes possible. The link is recorded so the treatment attaches to the mechanism it mitigates the consequences of.

evidence.snippet: Because hearing loss may be severe, initial use of hearing aids and/or assistive communication methods may be needed.
evidence.explanation: The GeneReviews recommendation for the auditory component.

treatments/1.description: Hearing loss is often the first and sometimes the most disabling feature, and because it arrives before the dementia it is the one deficit that can be meaningfully supported while the patient can still use the support.

evidence.snippet: Sedative or antipsychotic drugs help to reduce extreme restlessness, roaming behavior, delusions, and hallucinations associated with dementia.
evidence.explanation: The GeneReviews management statement, naming the drug classes and the symptoms they address.

treatments/2.description:
Symptomatic, and directed at the neuropsychiatric end of the disease rather than at the neuropathy. GeneReviews names sedative or antipsychotic drugs for the restlessness, roaming, delusions and hallucinations that accompany the dementia. This is the treatment for two phenotypes this entry already curates - Dementia and Auditory or visual hallucinations - which previously had none.
No agent, dose or trial is named in the source, and none should be inferred here. The recommendation is a class-level statement of what helps, not evidence that a particular drug was studied in this disease.

treatments/2/targets/0.description: The link is symptomatic, not disease-modifying. These drugs do not slow the cortical degeneration; they manage the behavioural disturbance that the degeneration produces.

evidence.snippet: Because behavioral changes and the loss of insight and judgment often present a considerable burden for partners or other caregivers, information about the disorder and psychological support for partners or other caregivers are essential.
evidence.explanation: The GeneReviews statement, including the reason the burden falls where it does.

treatments/3.description: GeneReviews calls this essential rather than optional, and the reason is specific to this disease: loss of insight and judgment means the burden falls on partners and carers at exactly the point the patient stops being able to describe what is happening. Recorded as a treatment rather than as a note because the source places it in MANAGEMENT alongside the drugs.

evidence.snippet: Hearing loss treatment by cochlear implantation is helpful and should be considered.
evidence.explanation: The authors' recommendation, drawn from the single implanted case below.

evidence.snippet: Two months after surgery, she started participating in conversations and reported to hear the neighbors' dog barking across the street, something she could not do previously.
evidence.explanation: The measured outcome in a genetically confirmed patient. A single case, which is why the claim here is that implantation worked in this patient rather than that it works in this disease.

evidence.snippet: Her experience also indicated that an early implantation before significant cognitive decline is likely to have more beneficial effects on quality of life.
evidence.explanation: The timing constraint, and the reason this intervention cannot simply be deferred: the benefit is bounded by the dementia that follows the hearing loss.

treatments/4.description:
The one intervention in this entry with a measured outcome in a genetically confirmed patient rather than a class recommendation. A woman with the de novo p.T497P variant and bilateral severe sensorineural hearing loss received a left cochlear implant at age 38 and her audiograms improved dramatically; she began participating in conversations again.
The caveat is as important as the result and is the authors' own. Her memory decline continued and limited the benefit, and they conclude that implantation before significant cognitive decline is likely to help more. That makes this a time-dependent intervention in a disease whose hearing loss arrives one to two decades before the dementia - which is the window this entry's progression section describes.

evidence.snippet: To date, two phenotypes produced by DNMT1 mutations have been reported, including hereditary sensory and autonomic neuropathy (HSAN) type IE with mutations in exon 20, and autosomal dominant cerebellar ataxia, deafness, and narcolepsy caused by mutations in exon 21.
evidence.explanation: States the exon-to-phenotype correlation in its standard form.

evidence.snippet: Our findings suggest that mutation in exon 21 of DNMT1 may also produce a HSAN phenotype.
evidence.explanation: The same paper's own counterexample to the rule it just stated. Recorded as REFUTE against the positional hypothesis, from a source that supports the hypothesis's premise.

evidence.snippet: Because all reported mutations of DNMT1 are concentrated in exons 20 and 21, which encode the replication focus targeting sequence (RFTS) domain of Dnmt1, the RFTS domain could be a mutation hot spot.
evidence.explanation: The shared-domain premise both phenotypes rest on.

evidence.snippet: One family carried previously identified mutation Tyr495Cys; the other carried a novel Tyr495His, both in the TS domain.
evidence.explanation: Two kindreds with different substitutions at the same residue, which is the finest-grained version of the position question.

evidence.snippet: Our results indicate that all the mutations causal for HSAN1E are located in the middle part or N-terminus end of the TS domain, whereas all the mutations causal for autosomal dominant cerebellar ataxia, deafness and narcolepsy are located in the C-terminus end of the TS domain.
evidence.explanation: The strongest statement of the positional rule, from the largest cohort - nine kindreds, 45 affected subjects - and framed by sub-domain position rather than by exon, which is what makes it survive the exon 21 counterexample.

evidence.snippet: Exome and direct sequencing studies disclosed two different point mutations affecting exon 21 of DNMT1 gene in patients with ADCA-DN, a novel heterozygous point mutation in exon 20 in two affected HSAN IE siblings, and a trinucleotide deletion in exon 20 in the latter patient with HSAN IE.
evidence.explanation: Independent segregation of exon 20 with HSAN1E and exon 21 with ADCA-DN across four families.

evidence.snippet: Phenotypic characterization pinpoints that ADCA-DN and HSAN IE represent two discrete clinical entities belonging to the same disease spectrum, with variable degree of overlap.
evidence.explanation: The nosological conclusion this entry follows in curating the two separately while recording the spectrum, from the study that phenotyped both most deeply.

hypotheses/0.description:
HSAN1E and ADCA-DN are allelic - both are caused by DNMT1 targeting-sequence domain variants - and the usual summary is that exon 20 gives HSAN1E and exon 21 gives ADCA-DN. GeneReviews treats them as one phenotypic spectrum rather than two diseases, which is the same observation from the other direction.
The correlation is not clean. A Japanese patient with an exon 21 variant (p.His569Arg) presented with the HSAN phenotype and no definite cerebellar ataxia. A separate DNMT1 variant has been reported with an overlapping phenotype spanning both syndromes. And narcolepsy, once treated as the ADCA-DN discriminator, has been found to be common in HSAN1E as well. Meanwhile two HSAN1E kindreds with canonical targeting-sequence variants had no narcolepsy at all, and one showed prominent psychiatric features and seizures with later onset than previously reported cases.
The strongest version of the rule is not about exons at all but about position within the domain. A nine-kindred, 45-subject cohort found every HSAN1E mutation in the middle or N-terminal end of the targeting-sequence domain and every ADCA-DN mutation at its C-terminal end - a finer and more mechanistically plausible statement than the exon 20 / exon 21 shorthand, and one the exon 21 HSAN case does not straightforwardly contradict, since exon boundaries and domain sub-regions are not the same partition.
So position within the domain is a real gradient rather than a rule with a counterexample, but what it controls - why an N-terminal lesion takes the sensory neurons and a C-terminal one the cerebellum - is unresolved. This entry is curated as a distinct Disease from ADCA-DN on clinical grounds, which is also how the deepest phenotyping study of both describes them: two discrete clinical entities in one spectrum, overlapping to a variable degree.

evidence.snippet: Importantly, pathway analysis revealed 1693 genes associated with the identified DMRs were highly associated in diverse neurological disorders and NAD+/NADH metabolism pathways is implicated in the pathogenesis.
evidence.explanation: A candidate route from the methylome change to neuronal vulnerability. This is a pathway enrichment over differentially methylated regions, not a demonstrated mechanism, and is treated accordingly.

evidence.snippet: However, the pathophysiological trajectories underlying these neurological disorders caused by DNMT1 mutations remain mostly unknown.
evidence.explanation: The explicit statement that the mechanism is unresolved, which is why this is recorded as a hypothesis rather than as pathophysiology.

hypotheses/1.description:
DNMT1's canonical job is copying the methylation pattern onto newly replicated DNA, which postmitotic neurons do not do. Yet the enzyme is highly expressed in adult neurons, and the disease is a neurodegeneration with no reported phenotype in the rapidly dividing tissues one would expect a maintenance methylation defect to hit first.
Candidate explanations available in the literature cited here: the methylome analysis found that genes associated with differentially methylated regions were enriched for neurological disorders and implicated NAD+/NADH metabolism; the cellular work found apoptosis-proneness and failed neuronal differentiation, suggesting the lesion may act during neurogenesis rather than only in mature neurons. Neither has been shown to be the operative mechanism in patients, and the authors of the cellular study say so directly.

evidence.snippet: Both variants lead to loss of function (LoF), which is demonstrated by aberrant splicing resulting in the complete absence of the CAPNS1 protein in affected patients.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the molecular lesion this node names, namely complete absence of the CAPNS1 protein through aberrant splicing.

evidence.snippet: The calpain holoenzyme was previously linked to pulmonary vascular development and progression of PAH in patients.
evidence.explanation: Records the prior link between calpain and pulmonary vascular biology that the authors invoke; the sentence restates earlier work rather than this study's own result.

steps/12.description: Biallelic loss-of-function CAPNS1 variants act through aberrant splicing and abolish the calpain small regulatory subunit entirely. The steps between absent CAPNS1 protein and pulmonary vascular disease are not established in the report that defines this subtype, so this node is linked directly to the pulmonary arterial hypertension phenotype rather than to a specific intervening remodeling step.

evidence.snippet: Mutations in the type II bone morphogenetic protein receptor (BMPR2) gene dramatically increase the risk of developing heritable PAH.
evidence.explanation: This establishes impaired BMPR2/BMP signaling as the canonical inherited trigger.

evidence.snippet: BMPR2 is the most prevalent PAH gene, found in over 80% of heritable cases.
evidence.explanation: This modern BMP-focused review supports the centrality of BMPR2/BMP pathway insufficiency in HPAH.

evidence.snippet: Changes in the pulmonary vasculature caused by the disruption of BMPR2 signaling are observed in three main vascular components; endothelial cells, smooth muscle cells, and fibroblasts.
evidence.explanation: This review shows that BMPR2 pathway disruption acts across the key vascular cell compartments.

steps/13.description: Germline defects centered on BMPR2 and related pathway components reduce protective BMP/TGF-beta signaling in pulmonary vascular cells, creating the upstream disease trigger for HPAH. Five of this entry's genes act within this axis and are bound here: BMPR2 as the type II receptor, GDF2 as a BMP ligand gene, SMAD9 as a downstream transcriptional effector, and ACVRL1 and ENG as the ALK1/endoglin receptor pair. A germline lesion at any of these steps lowers pathway output at this node.

evidence.snippet: Metabolic abnormalities include hyperglycolytic reprogramming, mitochondrial dysfunction, aberrant polyamine and sphingosine metabolism, reduced insulin sensitivity, and defective iron handling.
evidence.explanation: This review directly supports metabolic rewiring as a distinct mechanistic layer in BMPR2-linked PAH affecting vascular cell function.

steps/14.description: Pulmonary arterial endothelial cells undergo a Warburg-like shift toward glycolysis with impaired mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation, reducing energy availability and increasing reactive oxygen species that amplify dysfunction and apoptotic loss.

evidence.snippet: animal models suggests endothelial cell dysfunction
evidence.explanation: This review directly supports endothelial dysfunction and the apoptosis-selection sequence as an early mechanistic step.

evidence.snippet: Here, CAV1-silenced primary human pulmonary artery endothelial cells (PAECs) were proliferative and hypermigratory, with reduced cytoskeletal stress fibers.
evidence.explanation: Places the CAV1 product in this node's compartment - removing it from primary human pulmonary artery endothelial cells produces the proliferative, dysregulated endothelial phenotype the node describes.

evidence.snippet: The Bayesian inference approach allowed us to independently validate KDR, which encodes for the Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor Receptor 2 (VEGFR2), as a novel PAH candidate gene.
evidence.explanation: Identifies the KDR product as VEGFR2 and validates the gene in PAH. Note the limit of this quote: it establishes gene and product identity, not that VEGFR2 acts in the pulmonary arterial endothelium, which is why the KDR binding on this node is weaker than the SOX17 and ATP13A3 ones beside it.

evidence.snippet: In large-scale genomic studies, Sox17, an endothelial-specific transcription factor, has been suggested as a putative causal gene of pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH); however, its role and molecular mechanisms remain to be elucidated.
evidence.explanation: Places the SOX17 product in the endothelial compartment this node describes; the sentence restates the human genomic finding rather than this paper's own mouse experiments.

evidence.snippet: In adult mice, Sox17 deletion in pulmonary endothelial cells (ECs) induced PAH under hypoxia with high penetrance and severity, but not under normoxia.
evidence.explanation: Shows that removing SOX17 from the pulmonary endothelium alone is sufficient to produce the disease, supporting this node as the compartment in which SOX17 loss acts.

evidence.snippet: Functionally, loss of ATP13A3 was associated with reduced EC proliferation, increased apoptosis in serum starvation, and increased monolayer permeability to thrombin.
evidence.explanation: Places the ATP13A3 lesion at this endothelial node, including the apoptotic component the node describes, rather than at the smooth-muscle node.

evidence.snippet: The assessment of five PAH-associated missense ATP13A3 variants (L675V, M850I, V855M, R858H, and L956P) confirmed loss-of-function phenotypes represented by impaired polyamine transport and dysregulated EC function.
evidence.explanation: Confirms that the PAH-associated ATP13A3 alleles are loss-of-function for polyamine transport and disturb endothelial function.

steps/15.description: Pulmonary arterial endothelial cells show early dysfunction, impaired vasodilator production, and an apoptosis-to-apoptosis-resistant transition that seeds maladaptive vascular remodeling. CAV1 (caveolar signaling scaffold), KDR (VEGFR2) and SOX17 (endothelial-restricted transcription factor) are the HPAH genes whose products act within this endothelial compartment, together with ATP13A3, a polyamine transporter whose loss in endothelial cells reduces proliferation and increases apoptosis.

evidence.snippet: Metabolic abnormalities include hyperglycolytic reprogramming, mitochondrial dysfunction, aberrant polyamine and sphingosine metabolism, reduced insulin sensitivity, and defective iron handling.
evidence.explanation: This review directly supports metabolic rewiring as a distinct mechanistic layer in BMPR2-linked PAH affecting vascular cell function.

evidence.snippet: A cancer-like increase in cell proliferation and resistance to apoptosis reflects acquired abnormalities of mitochondrial metabolism and dynamics.
evidence.explanation: This independently supports mitochondrial-metabolic changes driving a proliferative, apoptosis-resistant phenotype in vascular cells.

steps/16.description: Pulmonary artery smooth muscle cells undergo metabolic reprogramming with increased glycolysis and mitochondrial dysfunction that supports proliferation and apoptosis resistance, driving vascular wall expansion.

evidence.snippet: Disease pathogenesis is driven by progressive remodeling of peripheral pulmonary arteries, caused by the excessive proliferation of vascular wall cells, including endothelial cells, smooth muscle cells and fibroblasts, and perivascular inflammation.
evidence.explanation: This review supports excessive smooth-muscle and other vascular-wall-cell proliferation as a core remodeling engine.

evidence.snippet: This gene subfamily is constitutively active at physiological resting membrane potentials in excitable cells, including smooth muscle cells, and has been particularly linked to the human pulmonary circulation.
evidence.explanation: Supports binding KCNK3 at the smooth-muscle node by placing TASK-1 activity at the resting membrane potential of smooth muscle cells in the pulmonary circulation.

evidence.snippet: Recent studies show that modulation of TASK-1 channels, either directly or indirectly by targeting their regulatory mechanisms, has the potential to control pulmonary arterial tone in humans.
evidence.explanation: Links TASK-1 channel activity to pulmonary arterial tone, the vasoconstrictive half of this node's claim.

steps/17.description: Pathologic signaling from dysfunctional endothelium and impaired BMP tone promotes pulmonary artery smooth muscle proliferation, narrowed vascular lumens, and increased vasoconstrictive responsiveness. KCNK3 encodes the TASK-1 two-pore-domain potassium channel, which is constitutively active at the resting membrane potential of smooth muscle cells and whose modulation can control pulmonary arterial tone; it is therefore bound at this smooth-muscle node rather than at the BMP trigger node.

evidence.snippet: in lung biopsies from PAH patients, virtually all lineages of inflammatory cells were detected in proximity to the remodeled pulmonary vasculature
evidence.explanation: This review supports perivascular inflammatory-cell accumulation as a direct human PAH pathologic feature.

evidence.snippet: The disruption of BMPR2 signaling pathway causes an increased degree of inflammation and decreases the ability of the immune system to resolve it.
evidence.explanation: This links BMPR2-related inherited disease biology to amplified and poorly resolved inflammation.

steps/18.description: Cytokine, chemokine, and immune-cell accumulation around pulmonary vessels amplifies remodeling and may be exaggerated in BMPR2-deficient vascular biology.

evidence.snippet: Genomic variation within the T-box 4 (TBX4) transcription factor is the second most common genetic cause of pulmonary arterial hypertension and can also cause severe lung developmental disorders with neonatal pulmonary hypertension (PH).
evidence.explanation: Establishes TBX4 as a major human HPAH gene whose phenotype spans lung developmental disorders; the sentence restates the established human genetics rather than this paper's own mouse work.

evidence.snippet: Therefore, we generated Tbx4 conditional knockout (Tbx4-CKO) mice in which Cre recombinase deletes exon 5 of Tbx4 within the embryonic lung mesenchyme to create a null allele.
evidence.explanation: Identifies the lung mesenchyme as the compartment in which Tbx4 loss was produced, supporting the cell type bound on this node.

evidence.snippet: These lungs also show a 39.3% decrease in von Willebrand factor-positive vessels and a 14.2% increase in vessel wall thickness.
evidence.explanation: Measures the reduced pulmonary vascular density and increased wall thickness that this node asserts.

steps/19.description: Loss of the TBX4 transcription factor in lung mesenchyme disturbs postnatal lung growth and the pulmonary vascular bed, producing airspace enlargement, fewer pulmonary vessels and thicker vessel walls. This is a developmental lesion rather than a lesion of BMP/TGF-beta signal transduction, and it is the mechanism by which the developmental-regulator arm of HPAH reaches pulmonary vascular disease.

evidence.snippet: In PAH, the pulmonary vasculature is dynamically obstructed by vasoconstriction, structurally obstructed by adverse vascular remodeling, and pathologically non-compliant as a result of vascular fibrosis and stiffening.
evidence.explanation: This review directly supports the occlusive, fibrotic, and stiffened vascular-remodeling state.

steps/20.description: The combined effects of endothelial dysfunction, smooth-muscle proliferation, fibrosis, and inflammation progressively obstruct the pulmonary vascular bed and raise pulmonary vascular resistance.

evidence.snippet: In some patients, maladaptive changes in the right ventricle, including ischemia and fibrosis, reduce right ventricular function and cause right ventricular failure.
evidence.explanation: This review supports the terminal right-ventricular maladaptation step in progressive PAH.

steps/21.description: Chronic right-ventricular afterload from obstructive pulmonary vascular disease causes hypertrophy, maladaptive remodeling, and eventual right heart failure.

evidence.snippet: Pulmonary arterial hypertension leads to significant impairment in haemodynamics, right heart function, exercise capacity, quality of life and survival.
evidence.explanation: This treatment review confirms the core hemodynamic disease phenotype and its major physiologic consequences.

steps/22.description: Pre-capillary pulmonary arterial hypertension is the defining hemodynamic phenotype of HPAH.

evidence.snippet: Patients with PAH have dyspnea, reduced exercise capacity, exertional syncope, and premature death from right ventricular failure.
evidence.explanation: The PAH review directly lists dyspnea among the major clinical manifestations.

steps/23.description: Progressive dyspnea is a common presenting symptom as pulmonary vascular resistance and right-heart burden rise.

evidence.snippet: Patients with PAH have dyspnea, reduced exercise capacity, exertional syncope, and premature death from right ventricular failure.
evidence.explanation: The review explicitly identifies exertional syncope as a characteristic PAH symptom.

steps/24.description: Exertional syncope reflects inadequate cardiac output during advanced pulmonary vascular disease.

evidence.snippet: In some patients, maladaptive changes in the right ventricle, including ischemia and fibrosis, reduce right ventricular function and cause right ventricular failure.
evidence.explanation: This directly supports right-ventricular failure as a major downstream clinical manifestation.

steps/25.description: Right ventricular failure is a late consequence of chronic pulmonary vascular overload.

evidence.snippet: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a rare and life-threatening vascular disorder, characterised by abnormal remodelling of the pulmonary vessels and elevated pulmonary artery pressure, leading to right ventricular hypertrophy and right-sided heart failure.
evidence.explanation: This review directly supports right-ventricular hypertrophy as a core downstream phenotype.

steps/26.description: Right ventricular hypertrophy reflects the compensated phase of chronic pressure overload before overt right-heart failure.

evidence.snippet: Patients with PAH have dyspnea, reduced exercise capacity, exertional syncope, and premature death from right ventricular failure.
evidence.explanation: The PAH review supports exercise intolerance through reduced exercise capacity.

steps/27.description: Reduced exercise tolerance tracks worsening cardiopulmonary reserve in progressive HPAH.

edges/12.description: Loss of protective BMP signaling destabilizes endothelial homeostasis.

edges/13.description: Reduced BMP signaling releases anti-proliferative constraints on smooth muscle cells.

edges/14.description: Endothelial dysfunction augments pathological smooth-muscle signaling.

edges/15.description: Smooth-muscle expansion contributes directly to lumen loss and resistance.

edges/16.description: Metabolic stress and ROS amplify endothelial dysfunction and apoptotic selection.

edges/17.description: Metabolic reprogramming directly supports smooth-muscle proliferation and survival.

edges/18.description: Inflammatory mediators intensify remodeling and stiffness of the pulmonary vascular wall.

edges/19.description: Progressive pulmonary vascular resistance increases right-ventricular afterload.

evidence.snippet: Obstructive pulmonary vascular remodeling in PAH increases right ventricular afterload causing right ventricular hypertrophy.
evidence.explanation: States the afterload-to-hypertrophy step this edge asserts.

edges/20.description: Raised right-ventricular afterload from obstructive remodeling produces right ventricular hypertrophy.

evidence.snippet: In some patients, maladaptive changes in the right ventricle, including ischemia and fibrosis, reduce right ventricular function and cause right ventricular failure.
evidence.explanation: States the maladaptation-to-failure step this edge asserts.

edges/21.description: Maladaptive right-ventricular remodeling reduces right-ventricular function and produces overt right heart failure.

evidence.snippet: Patients with PAH have dyspnea, reduced exercise capacity, exertional syncope, and premature death from right ventricular failure.
evidence.explanation: The review lists dyspnea among the clinical features of PAH in the same sentence that attributes death to right ventricular failure; attributing the symptom specifically to this node is an inference step, hence INDIRECT.

edges/22.description: Breathlessness is the dominant exertional symptom of the limited right-ventricular output this node describes.

evidence.snippet: Patients with PAH have dyspnea, reduced exercise capacity, exertional syncope, and premature death from right ventricular failure.
evidence.explanation: The review lists reduced exercise capacity among the clinical features of PAH; attributing it specifically to right-ventricular limitation is an inference step, hence INDIRECT.

edges/23.description: Reduced exercise capacity follows from the inability to raise cardiac output across the obstructed pulmonary circulation.

evidence.snippet: Patients with PAH have dyspnea, reduced exercise capacity, exertional syncope, and premature death from right ventricular failure.
evidence.explanation: The review names exertional syncope as a clinical feature of PAH; attributing it specifically to right-ventricular output limitation is an inference step, hence INDIRECT.

edges/24.description: Exertional syncope reflects a right ventricle unable to increase output to meet demand.

evidence.snippet: Our results show that disruption of Tbx4 expression during early lung development is sufficient to disrupt postnatal lung development and circulation.
evidence.explanation: States that the developmental lesion is sufficient to disturb the pulmonary circulation, which is the edge asserted here.

edges/25.description: Fewer and thicker-walled pulmonary vessels raise pulmonary vascular resistance; in the conditional knockout this was accompanied by a measured rise in right ventricular systolic pressure.

evidence.snippet: We demonstrated that biallelic LoF variants in CAPNS1 can cause idiopathic PAH by the complete absence of CAPNS1 protein.
evidence.explanation: States the causal claim that this edge encodes.

edges/26.description: Complete absence of the calpain small subunit is reported as a cause of pulmonary arterial hypertension; the intervening pulmonary vascular steps are not established for this gene.

evidence.snippet: mutation in the bone morphogenetic protein receptor 2 (BMPR2) gene has been identified as the main genetic cause of PAH
evidence.explanation: This review directly supports BMPR2 as the principal disease gene in heritable PAH.

evidence.snippet: In families known to harbor BMPR2 mutations, approximately 27% of individuals with a known genetic mutation in BMPR2 will develop detectable PAH.
evidence.explanation: This quantifies the incomplete penetrance of BMPR2-associated HPAH and is relevant for genetic counseling.

genes/0.notes: BMPR2 loss-of-function amplifies endothelial, smooth-muscle, inflammatory, and metabolic abnormalities that drive canonical HPAH pathogenesis.

evidence.snippet: a small proportion of familial PAH cases not due to BMPR2 mutations are explained by mutations in the genes associated with hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia (HHT)—activin-like kinase type 1 (ALK1) and Endoglin (ENG).
evidence.explanation: This review supports ACVRL1 as an HHT-associated hereditary PAH gene.

genes/1.notes: ACVRL1 variants define an overlap subgroup in which pulmonary arterial hypertension coexists with hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia (HHT) biology via dysregulated ALK1/endoglin/TGF-beta signaling.

evidence.snippet: a small proportion of familial PAH cases not due to BMPR2 mutations are explained by mutations in the genes associated with hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia (HHT)—activin-like kinase type 1 (ALK1) and Endoglin (ENG).
evidence.explanation: This review supports ENG as an HHT-overlap hereditary PAH gene.

genes/2.notes: ENG variants cause HHT-overlapping HPAH, reflecting the role of endoglin in endothelial homeostasis and protection against proliferative remodeling.

evidence.snippet: mutations in the gene TBX4 have been more closely studied in children than in adults; early work suggests that the prevalence is higher among pediatric than among adult PAH patients.
evidence.explanation: This review supports TBX4 as a developmental gene associated with pediatric and early-onset PAH.

genes/3.notes: TBX4 defects broaden HPAH pathogenesis beyond the classic BMPR2-centered model and point to disordered vascular development as an upstream mechanism.

evidence.snippet: mutations in the gene KCNK3 (Potassium Channel, Subfamily K, Member 3), which encodes the human TASK-1 protein, were initially discovered in three unrelated PAH families and three IPAH patients.
evidence.explanation: This review supports KCNK3 as a heritable PAH channelopathy gene.

genes/4.notes: KCNK3-associated disease highlights a channelopathy component within the broader heritable PAH spectrum and implicates ion-channel biology in pulmonary vascular control.

evidence.snippet: Mutations in the caveolin-1 (CAV1) gene were the initial discovery in the current next-generation sequencing era via the use of whole exome sequencing.
evidence.explanation: This review supports CAV1 as a rare hereditary PAH gene affecting caveolar signaling.

genes/5.notes: CAV1 defects impair caveolar-mediated cellular uptake and signaling, predisposing to endothelial dysfunction and vascular remodeling.

evidence.snippet: mutations in SMAD9, which is located on chromosome 13, have been described in PAH by a few reports.
evidence.explanation: This review supports SMAD9 as a rare BMP-pathway gene associated with PAH.

genes/6.notes: SMAD9 variants disrupt the canonical BMP/TGF-beta transcriptional cascade, linking PAH to impaired bone morphogenetic protein signal transduction.

evidence.snippet: Regarding the GDF2 variants, there was one likely pathogenic nonsense variant (c.259C>T, p. Gln87*) and two missense variants (c.1207G>A, p. Val403Ile; c.38T>C, p. Leu13Pro).
evidence.explanation: This cohort supports recurrent GDF2 variants in idiopathic/heritable PAH.

genes/7.notes: GDF2 defects reduce availability of a key protective BMP ligand, shifting the balance toward pathological rather than homeostatic BMP signaling in pulmonary vasculature.

evidence.snippet: In a total of 69 patients, the highest incidence of variants was found in the BMPR2, ATP13A3, and GDF2 genes.
evidence.explanation: This idiopathic/heritable PAH cohort supports ATP13A3 as one of the recurrent variant-bearing genes in PAH.

genes/8.notes: ATP13A3 expands the heritable PAH gene set beyond canonical BMP-pathway components and supports genetic heterogeneity within HPAH.

evidence.snippet: PAH due toSOX17pathogenic variants is a severe phenotype, frequently associated with CHD, haemoptysis and radiological abnormalities.
evidence.explanation: This cohort supports SOX17 as an HPAH gene with a severe, syndromic vascular phenotype.

genes/9.notes: SOX17-associated disease highlights a developmental-vascular subtype of HPAH with early onset, frequent congenital heart disease overlap, and abnormal thoracic vascular imaging.

evidence.snippet: We provide statistical evidence for an association between high impact, likely loss-of-function variants in KDR and significantly decreased KCO and later disease onset, further supported by familial segregation.
evidence.explanation: This genetic association study supports protein-truncating KDR variants as a PAH risk genotype with reduced KCO and later onset.

evidence.snippet: These findings suggest that loss-of-function variants in KDR are associated with a form of PAH characterized by a range of lung parenchymal abnormalities, including small airways disease, emphysema and ILD
evidence.explanation: This supports the distinctive PAH-plus-parenchymal-lung phenotype seen in KDR variant carriers.

genes/10.notes: KDR encodes VEGFR2 and implicates endothelial angiogenic signaling in a heritable PAH phenotype that overlaps with mild interstitial and emphysematous lung abnormalities.

evidence.snippet: the EIF2AK4 gene predispose to heritable pulmonary veno-occlusive
evidence.explanation: This review supports EIF2AK4 as the recessive PVOD/PCH overlap gene within the heritable pulmonary vascular disease spectrum.

genes/11.notes: EIF2AK4-associated disease overlaps biologically and clinically with pulmonary veno-occlusive disease and pulmonary capillary haemangiomatosis rather than classic autosomal-dominant arteriolar HPAH.

evidence.snippet: Both variants lead to loss of function (LoF), which is demonstrated by aberrant splicing resulting in the complete absence of the CAPNS1 protein in affected patients.
evidence.explanation: Establishes complete absence of the CAPNS1 protein as the molecular consequence of the reported alleles.

evidence.snippet: We demonstrated that biallelic LoF variants in CAPNS1 can cause idiopathic PAH by the complete absence of CAPNS1 protein.
evidence.explanation: States the authors' causal conclusion for biallelic CAPNS1 loss of function in pulmonary arterial hypertension.

genes/12.notes: CAPNS1 is the MONDO causal gene for "pulmonary hypertension, primary, 6" (MONDO:0958334, OMIM:620777). The ClinGen Gene-Disease Validity download of 2026-09-25 carries no CAPNS1 assertion, so no validity classification is available for this relationship.

evidence.snippet: Current therapies have mechanisms of action involving signalling via one of four pathways: endothelin-1, nitric oxide, prostacyclin and bone morphogenetic protein/activin signalling.
evidence.explanation: This review directly supports multi-pathway combination pharmacotherapy in PAH, including heritable disease.

treatments/0.description: Modern HPAH treatment uses combination pharmacotherapy directed at endothelin, nitric-oxide, prostacyclin, and BMP/activin signaling axes, with escalation based on risk and response.

steps/1.description: TNNT2 encodes cardiac troponin T, which anchors the troponin complex to tropomyosin on the thin filament and couples calcium binding by troponin C to the azimuthal movement of tropomyosin that exposes or occludes the myosin-binding sites on actin. Disease-associated TNNT2 missense variants concentrate in the tropomyosin-binding region, most classically Arg92Gln and Arg92Trp, and act as dominant poison peptides that are incorporated into the thin filament - even at low mutant fraction - rather than acting through simple loss of protein. This is the primary cardiomyocyte insult of CMH2.

evidence.snippet: Five TnT mutations (Δ14, Δ28 + 7, ΔE160, S179F and K273E) studied in recombinant troponin increased Ca(2+)-sensitivity and were all fully uncoupled.
evidence.explanation: Systematic in vitro survey of seven HCM-causing TNNT2 mutations showing calcium sensitization plus uncoupling as the consistent molecular signature.

evidence.snippet: Normalized pCa-tension relationships of R92Q and cTnT(DEL) fibres demonstrated a significant increase in sensitivity to Ca2+ at short (2.0 microm) and long (2.3 microm) sarcomere lengths (SL).
evidence.explanation: Direct skinned-fibre measurement of increased calcium sensitivity in transgenic R92Q myocardium at physiological sarcomere lengths.

evidence.snippet: cTnT-K280N hiPSC-CMs show elevated diastolic Ca2+ and increases in cell shortening. Impaired cardiomyocyte relaxation was only evident in homozygous cTnT-K280N hiPSC-CMs.
evidence.explanation: Extends the calcium-sensitization mechanism to isogenic CRISPR-edited human iPSC-cardiomyocytes, connecting it to elevated diastolic calcium and impaired relaxation.

steps/2.description: Mutant cardiac troponin T shifts the thin filament toward the calcium-bound, open regulatory state at lower calcium concentrations than wild type, raising myofilament calcium sensitivity - a consistent finding across the TNNT2 HCM alleles studied by in vitro motility, skinned-fibre, and hiPSC-cardiomyocyte assays. A second, mutation-recurring abnormality is uncoupling of calcium sensitivity from troponin I phosphorylation by protein kinase A, which normally lowers calcium sensitivity as part of the beta-adrenergic lusitropic response; several TNNT2 mutant troponins are unresponsive to this modulation, removing the physiological desensitization reserve.

evidence.snippet: These changes in Ca2+ handling resulted in beat-to-beat instability and triangulation of the cardiac action potential, which are predictors of arrhythmia risk.
evidence.explanation: Human CRISPR-edited I79N hiPSC-cardiomyocyte evidence directly linking the TNNT2-mutant calcium-handling defect to an electrophysiological arrhythmia substrate.

evidence.snippet: While wild-type (WT) hiPSC-CMs were accurately entrained to frequencies of at least 150 bpm, the I79N hiPSC-CMs demonstrated clear patterns of alternans for both V m and Ca2+ transients at frequencies >75 bpm.
evidence.explanation: Quantifies the rate-dependent electrophysiological instability (alternans) that emerges in I79N mutant cardiomyocytes well below the pacing rate tolerated by isogenic controls.

evidence.snippet: Mice expressing the I79N variant were particularly susceptible to ventricular tachycardia and arrhythmias that was coincident with an increased myofibrillar Ca2+ sensitivity, action potential triangulation, and increased dispersion of ventricular conduction velocities at fast heart rates in the absence of structural abnormalities.
evidence.explanation: Corroborates the electrophysiological mechanism in transgenic mice studied prior to any overt hypertrophy developing, establishing that the arrhythmic substrate is not downstream of, and can precede, structural remodeling.

steps/3.description: Because the calcium-sensitized thin filament buffers cytosolic calcium more avidly, the beat-to-beat cytosolic calcium transient is reduced and its decay altered, which destabilizes cardiomyocyte electrophysiology independent of any structural change. In human CRISPR-edited I79N hiPSC cardiomyocytes and in transgenic I79N/F110I/R278C mouse hearts, this manifests as beat-to-beat instability, action potential triangulation, and - at increasing pacing frequency - alternans of both membrane voltage and calcium transients, together with increased dispersion of ventricular conduction velocity. This electrophysiological branch is the direct mechanistic link between the calcium-handling lesion and the malignant arrhythmic phenotype, distinct from and largely independent of the degree of structural hypertrophy.

evidence.snippet: At short SL, Ca2+-activated maximal tension in both R92Q and cTnT(DEL) fibres decreased significantly (24 and 21 %, respectively; P < 0.005), with no corresponding decrease in Ca2+-activated maximal ATPase activity. Therefore, at short SL, the tension cost in R92Q and cTnT(DEL) fibres increased by 35 and 29 %, respectively (P < 0.001).
evidence.explanation: Quantifies the energetic inefficiency directly: ATP turnover is maintained while force generation falls, raising the tension cost of contraction in both TNNT2 mutant fibre types studied.

evidence.snippet: Echocardiography showed left ventricular hypertrophy, enhanced contractility, and diastolic dysfunction in both models; however, these phenotypes were more pronounced in the R92Q mice.
evidence.explanation: Documents enhanced (hypercontractile) function and diastolic dysfunction in both TNNT2 mouse models, with the R92Q allele showing the more severe phenotype.

evidence.snippet: The cTnT-K280N mutation increases myofilament Ca2+-sensitivity, elevates diastolic Ca2+, enhances contractility and impairs cellular relaxation.
evidence.explanation: Human patient-derived and isogenic hiPSC-cardiomyocyte confirmation that the calcium-sensitized thin filament produces cellular hypercontractility with impaired relaxation.

steps/4.description: The calcium-sensitized, uncoupled thin filament produces cardiomyocyte hypercontractility with a disproportionate rise in the energetic cost of tension generation: mutant fibres develop increased force per unit calcium but consume ATP inefficiently relative to the tension produced, and the magnitude of this energetic penalty scales with the fraction of mutant protein incorporated into the sarcomere. Downstream, mutation-specific secondary changes in excitation-contraction coupling (blunted inotropic reserve, slowed calcium-transient decay, altered SERCA function and CaMKII activity for the R92Q allele) compound the primary myofilament lesion, so cellular dysfunction in CMH2 is not attributable to the thin-filament defect alone.

evidence.snippet: The mean (+/- SD) maximal thickness of the left ventricular wall in subjects with cardiac troponin T mutations (16.7 +/- 5.5 mm) was significantly less than that in subjects with beta cardiac myosin heavy-chain mutations (23.7 +/- 7.7 mm, P < 0.001).
evidence.explanation: Directly quantifies the milder hypertrophy in TNNT2 mutation carriers compared with MYH7 mutation carriers in the same cohort.

steps/5.description: Chronic myofilament hypercontractility and calcium-dependent hypertrophic signaling drive cardiomyocyte hypertrophy, myofiber disarray, and interstitial fibrosis, the histological substrate common to hypertrophic cardiomyopathy generally. The distinguishing feature of CMH2 is that this remodeling is frequently mild or subclinical on echocardiography relative to carriers of MYH7 variants, even though the underlying myofilament defect and downstream arrhythmic risk are severe - the wall-thickness measurement systematically understates disease severity for many TNNT2 alleles.

evidence.snippet: These data support the observation that apparently diverse cardiac troponin T gene mutations produce a consistent disease phenotype. Because this is one of poor prognosis, despite deceptively mild or undetectable hypertrophy, genotyping at this locus may be particularly informative in patient management and counselling.

evidence.snippet: Variant-specific rather than gene-specific prognosis should be considered during sudden cardiac death risk assessment.

steps/6.description: The clinical hallmark of CMH2, first described for the Arg92 hotspot and confirmed in independent pedigrees, is a dissociation between the degree of left ventricular hypertrophy and the risk of sudden cardiac death: carriers of malignant TNNT2 alleles have a high incidence of sudden death, often at a young age, despite mild or even subclinical hypertrophy on imaging. This "malignant but mild" pattern means that wall-thickness-based risk stratification alone systematically underestimates risk for these carriers, and it is why genetic testing and genotype-specific counselling are emphasized for TNNT2 families. The pattern is allele-dependent rather than gene-wide: the founder variant p.Asn271Ile instead produces late-onset, low-risk disease, so risk assessment must be made at the level of the specific variant.

evidence.snippet: Missense mutations (Ile79Asn; Arg92Gln) and a mutation in the splice donor sequence of intron 15 of the cardiac troponin T gene are also shown to cause FHC.
evidence.explanation: The original gene-disease assertion establishing TNNT2 as causative for familial hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, including the founding Arg92Gln allele.

evidence.snippet: A novel cardiac troponin T gene mutation, arginine 92 tryptophan, was identified in 19 of 48 members of two affected pedigrees.
evidence.explanation: Independent confirmation of a second missense allele at the codon 92 hotspot cosegregating with disease in two large pedigrees.

evidence.snippet: TNNT2 | HGNC:11949 | hypertrophic cardiomyopathy | MONDO:0005045 | AD | Moderate

evidence.snippet: Late-onset HCM and incomplete age-related penetrance were observed (estimated median diagnosis age 60.1 years). ... Codon 92 variants' carriers (76 individuals, 28 probands) had a higher penetrance, being diagnosed 19.4 years earlier, and they exhibited a significantly worse prognosis (primary endpoint in 34.3%; P < 0.001).
evidence.explanation: Documents that TNNT2 genotype-phenotype correlation must be made at the allele level: the founder variant p.Asn271Ile is low-risk and late-onset, in direct contrast to the malignant codon-92 hotspot variants that define the classic CMH2 phenotype.

genes/0.notes: Disease-associated TNNT2 variants for CMH2 are overwhelmingly missense and concentrate in the tropomyosin-binding N-terminal and central regions of cardiac troponin T, with codon 92 (Arg92Gln, Arg92Trp, Arg92Pro/Leu) as the best-characterized hotspot for the malignant, minimal-hypertrophy phenotype. Other alleles cited in this entry with human genotype-phenotype data: Ile79Asn, K280N (reported homozygous), E163R, and the low-risk founder variant p.Asn271Ile. A splice-donor mutation in intron 15, predicted to act as a null allele, was among the original TNNT2 alleles reported and was used to argue that abnormal sarcomeric protein stoichiometry, not only a poison-peptide mechanism, can produce the phenotype.

evidence.snippet: The R92Q TnT mutation in troponin from transgenic mouse increased Ca(2+)-sensitivity and was also completely uncoupled.
evidence.explanation: Directly demonstrates both halves of the canonical mechanism - increased calcium sensitivity and uncoupling from troponin I phosphorylation - for the founding R92Q CMH2 allele.

evidence.snippet: Myofilament Ca2+-sensitivity was higher in homozygous cTnT-K280N cardiomyocytes and was not corrected by AP- and PKA-treatment. ... A low level (14%) of the cTnT-K280N sensitizes myofilaments to Ca2+, a universal finding of human HCM.
evidence.explanation: Human explanted-myocardium and isogenic hiPSC-cardiomyocyte study showing that even a low mutant protein fraction (14%) is sufficient to raise calcium sensitivity, and that PKA treatment does not correct it - corroborating the uncoupling component of the mechanism directly in human tissue rather than only in transgenic mice.

hypotheses/0.description: The canonical model of CMH2 is that HCM-associated TNNT2 variants are incorporated into the thin filament as poison peptides that increase myofilament calcium sensitivity - a near-universal finding across the disease-associated alleles studied to date, from the founder R92Q mutation in transgenic mice to recombinant and patient-derived troponin carrying K280N, DeltaE160, S179F, and other substitutions. A second, recurring feature specific to several TNNT2 (and other thin-filament) HCM mutations is "uncoupling": normal cardiac troponin I phosphorylation by protein kinase A lowers myofilament calcium sensitivity as part of the lusitropic (relaxation-enhancing) response to adrenergic stimulation, but mutant troponin T blunts or abolishes this modulation, removing a physiological brake on calcium sensitivity precisely when it is most needed.

evidence.snippet: In R92Q myocardium, we found a blunted response to inotropic interventions, slower decay of Ca2+ transients, reduced SERCA function, and increased Ca2+/calmodulin kinase II activity. Contrarily, secondary alterations of E-C coupling and signaling were minimal in E163R myocardium.
evidence.explanation: States the divergence explicitly: the R92Q model is dominated by excitation-contraction coupling remodeling while the E163R model is dominated by primary myofilament energetic abnormalities, both producing the shared HCM phenotype by different molecular routes.

evidence.snippet: Our data indicate that an important mutation-linked effect on cardiac function is the result of an inefficient use of ATP at the myofilament level. Furthermore, the extent of the mutation-induced dysfunction depends not only on the nature of the mutation, but also on the concentration of the mutant protein in the sarcomere.
evidence.explanation: Independent transgenic-mouse evidence that both which TNNT2 mutation is present and how much mutant protein is expressed determine the nature and severity of myofilament dysfunction. PARTIAL because it documents dose- and mutation-dependence in general rather than the specific myofilament/E-C-coupling divergence claimed by the R92Q/E163R comparison.

hypotheses/1.description: A second, complementary account holds that the relative contribution of primary myofilament dysfunction versus secondary excitation-contraction (E-C) coupling remodeling to the CMH2 phenotype is mutation-specific rather than uniform across the gene. In paired mouse models, the R92Q allele produced comparatively modest myofilament-level sarcomeric changes beyond calcium sensitization but profound secondary E-C coupling remodeling (blunted inotropic reserve, slowed calcium-transient decay, reduced SERCA function, increased CaMKII activity), whereas the E163R allele produced prominent primary myofilament abnormalities (altered sarcomere energetics, elevated resting tension) with comparatively preserved calcium handling. Both alleles converge on diastolic dysfunction and arrhythmogenicity, but by different routes, with implications for which class of therapy - sarcomere-targeting versus ion-channel/calcium-targeting - is mechanistically matched to a given carrier's genotype.

evidence.snippet: Hypophosphatasia (HPP) is a rare inherited metabolic disorder characterized by deficient activity of tissue-nonspecific alkaline phosphatase (TNAP) caused by variants in the ALPL gene.

steps/1.description: Loss-of-function variants in ALPL reduce tissue-nonspecific alkaline phosphatase (TNAP) activity. Because TNAP functions as both an alkaline phosphatase and a pyrophosphatase at physiological pH, reduced activity lowers circulating alkaline phosphatase and prevents normal hydrolysis of mineralization and vitamin B6 substrates.

evidence.snippet: elevated levels of ALP substrates, specifically inorganic pyrophosphate (PPi), pyridoxal 5'-phosphate (PLP) or urine phosphoethanolamine (PEA)

steps/2.description: Deficient TNAP causes accumulation of natural substrates, especially inorganic pyrophosphate (PPi), pyridoxal 5'-phosphate (PLP), and urinary phosphoethanolamine (PEA). PPi blocks apatite crystal growth, whereas PLP accumulation reflects disrupted vitamin B6 handling.

evidence.snippet: The skeletal disease is due to PP(i) inhibition of hydroxyapatite crystal growth extracellularly so that crystals form within matrix vesicles but fail to enlarge after these structures rupture.

evidence.snippet: TNAP plays a crucial role in biomineralization of bones and teeth, in part by reducing levels of inorganic pyrophosphate (PPi), an inhibitor of biomineralization.

steps/3.description: Excess PPi inhibits hydroxyapatite crystal growth after matrix vesicle rupture, producing defective mineralization of bone, growth plates, teeth, and the dentoalveolar complex. This mechanism accounts for rickets or osteomalacia, impaired growth, fractures, premature tooth loss, and severe chest-wall disease.

evidence.snippet: TNSALP is also necessary for proper vitamin B6 metabolism and its participation as a cofactor for neurotransmitters in the central nervous system.

steps/4.description: TNAP normally participates in vitamin B6 metabolism through extracellular PLP dephosphorylation. evidence.explanation: Gives the structural reason the splice allele is a null rather than a hypomorph, which is what places it in the complete-loss class.

evidence.explanation: Establishes that the truncating STWS2 alleles remove the receptor from the membrane rather than producing a signaling-competent stump.

steps/1.description: Biallelic essential loss-of-function IL6ST alleles — nonsense (c.841C>T, p.Arg281*), an intronic splice variant causing exon 13 skipping (c.1699+4A>G), and a further truncating allele (p.Ser375*) — abolish functional cell-surface GP130. The truncating alleles lie in the extracellular domains, so the predicted products are soluble rather than membrane-anchored receptor fragments; the exon-13 skipping allele instead misfolds the membrane-proximal D6 domain, which is where the receptor transmits signal across the membrane.

evidence.snippet: Functional tests showed absent cellular responses to GP130-dependent cytokines including IL-6, IL-11, IL-27, oncostatin M (OSM), and leukemia inhibitory factor (LIF).
evidence.explanation: Direct patient-cell readout that all five tested GP130-dependent cytokines fail, which is the defining property of this node.

evidence.snippet: Genetic reconstitution of GP130 by lentiviral transduction in patient-derived cells reversed the signaling defect.
evidence.explanation: Rescue experiment establishing that the signaling failure is caused by the IL6ST genotype rather than by a co-segregating factor.

evidence.snippet: The gene IL6ST encodes GP130, the common signal transducer of the IL-6 cytokine family consisting of 10 cytokines.
evidence.explanation: States why one receptor loss silences a whole cytokine family, which is the premise of this node.

evidence.snippet: Deletion of this membrane-proximal interaction site in GP130 consequently caused additional defective LIF signaling and Stüve-Wiedemann syndrome.
evidence.explanation: Structural work showing that losing LIF signaling on top of the IL-6/IL-11 defect is what converts an IL6ST hyper-IgE genotype into a Stuve-Wiedemann one — the boundary this node draws.

steps/2.description: GP130 is the shared transducer of the whole IL-6 cytokine family, so its complete loss silences every member at once — IL-6, IL-11, IL-27, oncostatin M and LIF have all been shown unresponsive in patient cells. This is the node that separates STWS2 from STWS1: LIFR loss removes only the LIF-receiving chain, leaving IL-6, IL-11 and IL-27 signaling intact. It also separates STWS2 from the IL6ST hyper-IgE and craniosynostosis phenotypes, which are cytokine-selective defects that spare LIF. Lentiviral reconstitution of GP130 in patient cells restores signaling, which is the strongest available evidence that the failure is the direct consequence of the genotype.

evidence.snippet: This study identifies a new genetic syndrome caused by the complete lack of signaling of a whole family of GP130-dependent cytokines in humans and highlights the importance of the LIF signaling pathway in pre- and perinatal development.

evidence.snippet: Similarities of patients with loss of LIFR signaling and patients that had complete absence of GP130 suggest that LIF is essential during embryonic development.

steps/3.description: Absent LIF-family signaling in the developing skeleton produces the bent-bone phenotype. steps/5.description: This node is what "extended" Stuve-Wiedemann syndrome means.
